title.zh: 卷二百一十一 列傳第一百三十六 藩鎮鎮冀
title.raw: 卷二百一十一 列傳第一百三十六 藩鎮鎮冀 Volume 211 Biographies 136: Buffer Region Zhenji

sentences.zh: 藩鎮鎮冀

translations.literal: Buffer region: Zhen-Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhen-Ji Buffer Region.

sentences.zh: 李寶臣字為輔，本范陽內屬奚也。

translations.literal: Li Baochen, style name Weifu, was originally a Xi tribesman subject to Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baochen, whose courtesy name was Weifu, was originally a Xi tribesman affiliated with Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 善騎射。

translations.literal: He excelled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 范陽將張鎖高畜為假子，故冒其姓，名忠誌。

translations.literal: The Fanyang general Zhang Suogao raised him as a nominal son, so he took that surname and was named Zhongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Fanyang commander Zhang Suogao adopted him as a foster son, and he accordingly took Zhang's surname and the personal name Zhongzhi.

sentences.zh: 為盧龍府果毅，常覘虜陰山，追騎及，射六人盡殪，乃還。

translations.literal: He served as a guoyi in the Lulong prefecture; he often scouted toward the Yin Mountains, and when pursuers caught up he shot down six men and returned.
translations.idiomatic: As a guoyi officer in the Lulong command, he often reconnoitered toward the Yin Mountains; when enemy riders overtook him, he killed six of them and made his way back.

sentences.zh: 為安祿山射生，從入朝，留為射生子弟，出入禁中。

translations.literal: He became a hunting officer for An Lushan, followed him to court, and was kept as a member of the hunting corps, entering and leaving the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He served An Lushan as a master of the hunt, accompanied him to the capital, and was retained in the imperial hunting corps with access to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，遁歸，更為祿山假子，使將驍騎十八人，劫太原尹楊光翙，挾以出，追兵萬餘不敢逼。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled he fled back, again became Lushan's nominal son, and was sent with eighteen elite horsemen to seize Taiyuan prefect Yang Guangbi and carry him off; more than ten thousand pursuers did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rose in rebellion, he slipped away and returned, was again made Lushan's foster son, and led eighteen crack horsemen to seize the Taiyuan prefect Yang Guangbi and escort him out; over ten thousand pursuers dared not close in.

sentences.zh: 又督精甲軍土門，以扼井陘。

translations.literal: He also commanded elite armored troops at Tumen to block the Jingxing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He also directed crack armored troops at Tumen to hold the Jingxing Pass.

sentences.zh: 事安慶緒為恒州刺史。

translations.literal: He served An Qingxu as prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under An Qingxu he served as prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 九節度師圍相州也，忠誌懼，歸命於朝，肅宗即授故官，封密雲郡公。

translations.literal: When the nine military commissioners besieged Xiangzhou, Zhongzhi grew afraid, submitted to the court, and Suzong at once restored his former office and enfeoffed him as Duke of Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies of nine commissioners besieged Xiangzhou, Zhongzhi, fearing for himself, defected to the court; Emperor Suzong immediately reappointed him to his former post and created him Duke of Miyun.

sentences.zh: 史思明度河，忠誌復叛，勒兵三萬固守，賊將辛萬寶屯恒州相掎角。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming crossed the river, Zhongzhi rebelled again, mustered thirty thousand men to hold fast, and the rebel general Xin Wanbao garrisoned Hengzhou in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Siming crossed the Yellow River, Zhongzhi rebelled once more, rallied thirty thousand troops for a stubborn defense, and coordinated with the rebel general Xin Wanbao, who held Hengzhou as a counterweight.

sentences.zh: 思明死，忠誌不肯事朝義，使裨將王武俊殺萬寶，挈恒、趙、深、定、易五州以獻。

translations.literal: When Siming died, Zhongzhi refused to serve Chaoyi, had his lieutenant Wang Wujun kill Wanbao, and presented the five prefectures of Heng, Zhao, Shen, Ding, and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After Siming's death, Zhongzhi would not submit to Chaoyi; he had his deputy Wang Wujun kill Wanbao and surrendered the five prefectures of Heng, Zhao, Shen, Ding, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 雍王東討，開土門納王師，助攻莫州。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yong marched east to punish the rebels, he opened Tumen and admitted the imperial army, then joined in the assault on Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Prince of Yong's eastern campaign, he opened Tumen to the imperial forces and took part in the attack on Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 朝義平，擢禮部尚書，封趙國公，名其軍曰成德，即拜節度使，賜鐵券許不死，它賫與不貲，賜姓及名。

translations.literal: When Chaoyi was pacified he was promoted to Minister of Rites, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, named his army Chengde, and was at once appointed military commissioner; he was granted an iron certificate promising he would not be put to death, along with other gifts beyond reckoning, and was given an imperial surname and name.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaoyi's defeat he was promoted to Minister of Rites, created Duke of Zhao, and gave his army the name Chengde; he was immediately appointed military commissioner, granted an iron certificate of immunity, showered with rewards beyond measure, and bestowed an imperial surname and personal name.

sentences.zh: 於是遂有恒、定、易、趙、深、冀六州地，馬五千，步卒五萬，財用豐衍，益招來亡命，雄冠山東。

translations.literal: He then held the six prefectures of Heng, Ding, Yi, Zhao, Shen, and Ji, with five thousand horses and fifty thousand infantry; his wealth was abundant, he increasingly recruited fugitives, and he was foremost in power east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He now controlled the six prefectures of Heng, Ding, Yi, Zhao, Shen, and Ji, with five thousand cavalry and fifty thousand foot soldiers; his resources were ample, he steadily drew in desperate men, and his might was unmatched in the east.

sentences.zh: 與薛嵩、田承嗣、李正己、梁崇義相姻嫁，急熱為表裹。

translations.literal: He intermarried with Xue Song, Tian Chengsi, Li Zhengji, and Liang Chongyi, and they were urgently intimate, inside and outside alike.
translations.idiomatic: He formed marriage alliances with Xue Song, Tian Chengsi, Li Zhengji, and Liang Chongyi, and they were bound together in the closest mutual dependence.

sentences.zh: 先是天寶中，玄宗冶金自為象，州率置祠，更賊亂，悉毀以為貲，而恒獨存，故見寵異，加賜實封。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Tianbao era, Xuanzong had metal cast into statues for himself; each prefecture generally set up shrines, but during the rebellions all were destroyed for cash except at Heng, which alone survived; for this he was shown special favor and given additional substantive fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao period, Emperor Xuanzong had statues cast in his likeness and each prefecture was expected to maintain a shrine; during the rebellions nearly all were melted down for money, but the one at Heng alone remained intact, and for this he received exceptional favor and an added substantive enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 始，寶臣與正己素為承嗣所易。

translations.literal: At first, Baochen and Zhengji had long been looked down upon by Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen and Zhengji had long been treated with contempt by Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 其弟寶正，承嗣婿也，往依魏，與承嗣子維擊球，馬駭，觸維死，承嗣怒，囚之，以告寶臣，寶臣謝教不謹，進杖，欲使示責，而承嗣遂鞭殺之，由是交惡。

translations.literal: His younger brother Baozheng, Chengsi's son-in-law, went to stay in Wei and played cuju with Chengsi's son Wei; a horse bolted, struck Wei, and killed him. Chengsi was enraged, imprisoned him, and informed Baochen; Baochen apologized for lax discipline and sent rods, intending to show censure, but Chengsi had him flogged to death, and from this they became enemies.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Baozheng, who was married into Chengsi's family, went to Wei and played cuju with Chengsi's son Wei; a horse panicked, struck Wei, and killed him. Chengsi flew into a rage, imprisoned Baozheng, and notified Baochen; Baochen apologized for poor discipline and sent whipping rods as a token of punishment, but Chengsi had Baozheng beaten to death anyway, and from that time the two were bitter foes.

sentences.zh: 乃與正己共劾承嗣可討狀。

translations.literal: He then joined Zhengji in memorializing that Chengsi was fit to be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhengji then jointly memorialized the throne with grounds for campaigning against Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 代宗欲其自相圖，則勢離易制，即詔寶臣與朱滔及太原兵攻其北，正己與滑亳、河陽、江淮兵攻其南。

translations.literal: Daizong wished them to fight one another so that, once divided, they would be easy to control; he therefore ordered Baochen with Zhu Tao and the Taiyuan troops to attack from the north, and Zhengji with the Hua-Bo, Heyang, and Jiang-Huai forces from the south.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong wanted them to tear one another apart so that, once split, they would be easier to manage; he accordingly ordered Baochen, Zhu Tao, and the Taiyuan army to strike from the north, while Zhengji advanced from the south with the Hua-Bo, Heyang, and Jiang-Huai troops.

sentences.zh: 師會棗強，椎牛饗軍，寶臣厚賜士，而正己頗觳，軍怨望，正己懼有變，即引去。

translations.literal: The armies met at Zaoqiang, slaughtered oxen to feast the troops; Baochen gave generous rewards to the soldiers, but Zhengji was rather stingy; the army grew resentful, Zhengji feared mutiny, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies assembled at Zaoqiang and slaughtered cattle for a feast, Baochen lavished rewards on the troops while Zhengji was notably tight-fisted; the men grew discontent, Zhengji feared a revolt, and pulled his forces away.

sentences.zh: 惟滔、寶臣攻滄州，歷年未下，擊宗城，殘之，斬二千級。

translations.literal: Only Tao and Baochen attacked Cangzhou; for years they could not take it; they struck Zongcheng, ravaged it, and beheaded two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Only Tao and Baochen pressed the siege of Cangzhou, which for years would not fall; they attacked Zongcheng, laid it waste, and took two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 承嗣弟廷琳方守貝州，遣高嵩巖將兵三千戍宗城，寶臣使張孝忠攻破之，斬嵩巖，逸所執將四十餘人。

translations.literal: Chengsi's younger brother Tinglin was then defending Beizhou; he sent Gao Songyan with three thousand men to garrison Zongcheng; Baochen had Zhang Xiaozhong break them, beheaded Songyan, and released more than forty captured officers.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi's brother Tinglin held Beizhou and sent Gao Songyan with three thousand men to garrison Zongcheng; Baochen sent Zhang Xiaozhong to defeat them, executed Songyan, and freed more than forty captured commanders.

sentences.zh: 會王武俊執賊大將盧子期，遂降洺、瀛。

translations.literal: When Wang Wujun captured the rebel great general Lu Ziqi, Luo and Ying surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun then captured the rebel commander Lu Ziqi, and the prefectures of Luo and Ying submitted.

sentences.zh: 當是時，河南諸將敗田悅於陳留，正己取德州，欲頗窮討。

translations.literal: At that time the generals south of the Yellow River defeated Tian Yue at Chenliu; Zhengji took Dezhou and wished to press the pursuit hard.
translations.idiomatic: About then the generals of the Henan front defeated Tian Yue at Chenliu; Zhengji seized Dezhou and wanted to drive the campaign to a finish.

sentences.zh: 承嗣懼，乃甘言紿正己，正己止屯，諸軍亦莫敢進。

translations.literal: Chengsi grew afraid and coaxed Zhengji with sweet words; Zhengji halted his encampment, and the other armies likewise dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi, alarmed, flattered Zhengji with smooth talk; Zhengji held his army in place, and the other columns dared not press forward either.

sentences.zh: 於是天子遣中人馬希倩勞寶臣，寶臣歸使者百縑，使者恚，抵諸道，寶臣顧左右愧甚。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven then sent the eunuch Ma Xiqian to reward Baochen; Baochen gave the envoy a hundred bolts of silk in return; the envoy was angry and spread the story through the circuits; Baochen looked to those beside him, deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then dispatched the eunuch Ma Xiqian to congratulate Baochen; Baochen sent the envoy away with a gift of a hundred bolts of silk; the envoy took offense and told the story everywhere; Baochen glanced at his attendants, utterly mortified.

sentences.zh: 諸將已休，獨武俊佩刀立所下，語之故。

translations.literal: The generals had already retired; only Wujun, wearing his sword, stood below the hall and told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals had already withdrawn; only Wujun, sword at his belt, remained below the hall and explained what had happened.

sentences.zh: 武俊計曰：「趙兵有功尚爾，使賊平，天子幅紙召置京師，一匹夫耳。」

translations.literal: Wujun reasoned, saying: "The Zhao troops have merit and are still treated thus; if the rebels are pacified, the Son of Heaven will summon you to the capital with a single sheet of paper—you will be no more than a common man.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun said, "Even with merit, the Zhao army is treated like this; once the rebels are crushed, the emperor will recall you to the capital with a single edict and you will be nothing but a private citizen.

sentences.zh: 曰：「奈何？」

translations.literal: He said, "What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Baochen asked, "What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「養魏以為資，上策也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "To nurture Wei as a resource is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: Wujun answered, "The best course is to keep Wei alive as your leverage."

sentences.zh: 寶臣曰：「趙、魏有釁，何從而可？」

translations.literal: Baochen said, "Zhao and Wei have a breach—how can this be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Baochen said, "Zhao and Wei are already at odds—how could that work?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「勢同患均，轉寇讎為父子，咳唾間耳。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your situations and dangers are the same; turning enemy into father and son is but the space of a cough or a spit.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "You share the same peril; turning sworn enemies into allies is the work of a moment.

sentences.zh: 朱滔屯滄州，請禽送魏，可以取信。」

translations.literal: Zhu Tao is stationed at Cangzhou; ask to capture and send him to Wei, and trust can be won."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao holds Cangzhou; offer to seize him and hand him over to Wei, and you will win their confidence."

sentences.zh: 寶臣然之。

translations.literal: Baochen agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen assented.

sentences.zh: 先是，承嗣知寶臣少長范陽，心常欲得之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chengsi knew that Baochen had grown up in Fanyang and had long wished to win him over.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi knew that Baochen had spent his youth in Fanyang and had long coveted his allegiance.

sentences.zh: 乃勒石若讖者瘞之境，教望氣者雲有王氣。

translations.literal: He therefore had a stone carved like a prophecy buried in the borderland and instructed geomancers to say there was royal qi.
translations.idiomatic: He had a stone inscribed like a prophecy buried on the frontier and coached diviners to declare that royal qi was present there.

sentences.zh: 寶臣掘得之，文曰：「二帝同功勢萬全，將田作伴入幽燕。」

translations.literal: Baochen dug it up; the text read: "Two emperors share merit and the situation is wholly secure; take Tian as companion and enter Youyan."
translations.idiomatic: Baochen unearthed it; the inscription read, "Two emperors share in merit and all is secure; take Tian as your partner and enter Youyan together.

sentences.zh: 「帝」謂寶臣與正己為二。

translations.literal: Emperors" meant Baochen and Zhengji as the two.
translations.idiomatic: The "two emperors" referred to Baochen and Zhengji.

sentences.zh: 而陰使客說曰：「公與滔共攻滄，即有功，利歸天子，公於何賴？

translations.literal: He secretly sent an agent to say: "If you and Tao jointly attack Cang, once there is merit the benefit goes to the Son of Heaven—what will you rely on?
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent an envoy who said, "If you and Tao take Cangzhou together, any glory will go to the throne—what will be left for you?

sentences.zh: 誠能赦承嗣罪，請奉滄州入諸趙，願取范陽以報。

translations.literal: If you can truly pardon Chengsi's crimes, he asks to present Cangzhou to join Zhao, and wishes to take Fanyang in return.
translations.idiomatic: If you will pardon Chengsi's offenses, he offers to surrender Cangzhou to Zhao and will seize Fanyang for you in repayment.

sentences.zh: 公以騎前驅，承嗣以步卒從，此萬全勢也。」

translations.literal: You lead with cavalry in front, Chengsi follows with infantry—this is a wholly secure position.
translations.idiomatic: You advance with cavalry while Chengsi follows with foot soldiers—a plan without flaw.

sentences.zh: 寶臣喜得滄州，又見語與讖會，遂陰交承嗣而圖幽州，承嗣陳兵出次以自驗。

translations.literal: Baochen was pleased to gain Cangzhou, and seeing the words match the prophecy, he then secretly allied with Chengsi to plot Youzhou; Chengsi arrayed troops and moved out to prove himself.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted at gaining Cangzhou and seeing the message match the prophecy, Baochen secretly aligned with Chengsi against Youzhou; Chengsi marched his army out to show good faith.

sentences.zh: 寶臣謬謂滔使曰：「吾聞朱公貌若神，願繪而觀可乎？」

translations.literal: Baochen falsely told Tao's envoy: "I have heard Lord Zhu's appearance is like a god's; might I have it painted to see?
translations.idiomatic: Baochen deceived Tao's envoy, saying, "They say Lord Zhu looks almost divine—may I have a portrait made to see for myself?

sentences.zh: 滔即圖以示之。

translations.literal: Tao at once had a picture made and showed it.
translations.idiomatic: Tao promptly had a likeness painted and sent it over.

sentences.zh: 寶臣置圖射堂，大會諸將，熟視曰：「信神人也！」

translations.literal: Baochen set the picture in the archery hall, gathered the generals in great assembly, studied it closely, and said: "Truly a divine man!
translations.idiomatic: Baochen hung the portrait in the archery hall, summoned his generals, gazed at it intently, and declared, "He truly looks like a god among men!

sentences.zh: 密選精卒二千，夜馳三百里欲劫滔，戒曰：「取彼貌如射堂者。」

translations.literal: He secretly chose two thousand elite troops, rode three hundred li by night intending to seize Tao, and warned: "Take the one whose face matches the archery hall."
translations.idiomatic: He secretly picked two thousand crack troops, galloped three hundred li through the night to abduct Tao, and ordered, "Seize whoever looks like the man in the archery hall."

sentences.zh: 時二軍不相虞，忽聞變，滔大駭，戰瓦橋，敗，衣佗服得脫，禽類滔者以歸承嗣。

translations.literal: At the time the two armies did not suspect each other; suddenly hearing of the upheaval, Tao was greatly alarmed; they fought at Waqiao; he was defeated, changed into another's clothes and escaped; one resembling Tao was captured and sent to Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: Neither army expected treachery; when the attack erupted Tao was terrified; at Waqiao he was beaten, swapped clothes with another man and slipped away, while someone who resembled him was seized and presented to Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 承嗣知釁成，還軍入堡，使人謝寶臣曰：「河內方有警，未暇從公。

translations.literal: Chengsi knew the breach was made, withdrew his army into the fort, and sent someone to apologize to Baochen, saying: "Within the passes there is suddenly an alarm; I have no leisure to follow you.
translations.idiomatic: Once the trap had worked, Chengsi pulled his troops back into his stronghold and sent word to Baochen: "There is trouble in the interior—I cannot join you just now.

sentences.zh: 石讖，吾戲為耳！」

translations.literal: The stone prophecy—I made it in jest!
translations.idiomatic: The stone prophecy was only a joke of mine!

sentences.zh: 寶臣慚而還。

translations.literal: Baochen withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Baochen marched home.

sentences.zh: 俄進封隴西郡王，又拜同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Prince of Longxi and also appointed Associate Director of the Secretariat with the rank of co-equal to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was promoted to Prince of Longxi and named Associate Director of the Secretariat with full ministerial standing.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，拜司空。

translations.literal: When Dezong acceded, he was appointed Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong came to the throne, Baochen was appointed Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 寶臣晚節尤猜忌，自顧子惟嶽且暗弱，恐下不服，即殺骨鯁將辛忠義、盧俶、許崇俊、張南容、張彭老等二十餘人，籍入其貲，眾乃攜貳。

translations.literal: In his later years Baochen was especially suspicious; seeing that his son Weiyue was dull and weak, he feared the subordinates would not submit, and so killed the outspoken generals Xin Zhongyi, Lu Chu, Xu Chongjun, Zhang Nanrong, Zhang Penglao, and more than twenty others, confiscating their property; the host then became divided in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years Baochen grew intensely paranoid; knowing his son Weiyue was dim and feeble, he feared the troops would not obey the heir and executed more than twenty stalwart commanders—including Xin Zhongyi, Lu Chu, Xu Chongjun, Zhang Nanrong, and Zhang Penglao—seizing their estates, until the army itself turned disloyal.

sentences.zh: 寶臣既貯異志，引妖人作讖兆，為丹書、靈芝、朱草，齋別室，築壇置銀盤、金匜、玉，猥曰：「內產甘露液神酒。」

translations.literal: Baochen, having harbored divergent ambitions, brought in sorcerers to produce omens, made red writing, lingzhi fungus, and crimson grass, fasted in a separate chamber, built an altar and set out silver trays, golden ladles, and jade, falsely saying: "Within are produced sweet-dew liquid and divine wine.
translations.idiomatic: Harbouring designs against the throne, Baochen enlisted sorcerers to manufacture portents—red scriptures, lingzhi mushrooms, crimson herbs—and kept a private fasting chamber with an altar furnished with silver dishes, golden cups, and jade, claiming falsely that "sweet dew and divine wine are produced within.

sentences.zh: 刻玉印，告其下曰：「天瑞自至。」

translations.literal: He carved a jade seal and told his subordinates: "Heavenly auspices come of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: He had a jade seal carved and told his followers, "Heaven sends its own omens."

sentences.zh: 眾莫敢辨者。

translations.literal: None dared dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared challenge him.

sentences.zh: 妖人復言：「當有玉印自天下，海內不戰而定。」

translations.literal: The sorcerer again said: "A jade seal will come down from heaven; within the seas all will be settled without battle.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer added, "A jade seal will descend from heaven and the realm will be pacified without a fight.

sentences.zh: 寶臣大悅，厚賫金帛。

translations.literal: Baochen was greatly pleased and richly rewarded him with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen was delighted and heaped gold and silk upon him.

sentences.zh: 既而畏事露且誅，詐曰：「公飲甘露液，可與天神接。」

translations.literal: Then, fearing exposure and execution, he falsely said: "If you, my lord, drink the sweet-dew liquid, you can commune with the heavenly spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing discovery and his own death, the sorcerer lied, "Drink the sweet dew, my lord, and you may commune with the gods.

sentences.zh: 密置堇於液，寶臣已飲即瘖，三日死，年六十四。

translations.literal: He secretly put aconite in the liquid; once Baochen had drunk he lost his voice, and died in three days, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly poisoned the draught with aconite; Baochen drank, was struck mute, and died three days later at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽悉誅殺妖人，時建中二年也。

translations.literal: Weiyue executed all the sorcerers; it was the second year of Jianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue had every sorcerer put to death; this was in the second year of the Jianzhong era.

sentences.zh: 遺表請以惟嶽領軍，詒書執政諉家事，歸節於朝，詔贈太傅。

translations.literal: His final memorial asked that Weiyue lead the army; a letter to the chief ministers shifted blame to family affairs and returned the commission to the court; an edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In his dying memorial he asked that Weiyue take command; a letter to the central ministers blamed domestic troubles and offered to return his commission to the court; the throne posthumously appointed him Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽少為行軍司馬、恒州刺史，寶臣死，軍中推為留後，求襲父位，帝不許。

translations.literal: Weiyue had earlier served as campaigning deputy and prefect of Hengzhou; when Baochen died the army pushed him as acting commissioner and sought to inherit his father's post; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue had served as campaigning deputy and prefect of Hengzhou; when Baochen died the troops made him acting commissioner and petitioned for him to succeed his father, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 趣護喪還京師，以張孝忠代之。

translations.literal: He was urged to escort the coffin back to the capital; Zhang Xiaozhong was appointed to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to return to the capital for the funeral while Zhang Xiaozhong was named to replace him.

sentences.zh: 田悅為請，不聽。

translations.literal: Tian Yue pleaded on his behalf; the court would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue interceded for him, but the court would not relent.

sentences.zh: 遂與悅、李正己謀拒命。

translations.literal: He then plotted with Yue and Li Zhengji to defy orders.
translations.idiomatic: He then conspired with Yue and Li Zhengji to resist the throne.

sentences.zh: 府小史胡震、私人王他奴等專畫反計。

translations.literal: The prefectural clerk Hu Zhen and the private retainer Wang Tanu and others alone drew up rebel plans.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk Hu Zhen and the household retainer Wang Tanu took charge of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 府屬邵真泣曰：「先公位將相，恩甚厚，而大夫違命缞绖中，愚固惑焉。

translations.literal: The staff member Shao Zhen wept and said: "Your late father stood as general and minister; the grace was very great, yet you, my lord, defy orders while still in mourning garb—I am truly perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: The staff officer Shao Zhen wept and said, "Your father rose to general and minister and received the deepest favor, yet you defy the court even while wearing mourning—I cannot understand it.

sentences.zh: 魏近且與國，不可遽絕，絕之速禍，請厚禮遣其使，徐更圖之；

translations.literal: Wei is near and still allied with the state; you cannot break off abruptly—breaking off brings swift disaster; please send their envoy away with generous gifts and plan more slowly;
translations.idiomatic: Wei is close at hand and still our ally; to break with them abruptly would invite disaster—treat their envoy generously and bide your time;

sentences.zh: 齊遠而交疏，不如械使者送京師，且請致討。

translations.literal: Qi is far and the tie is loose; better to fetter the envoy and send him to the capital, and also request punitive action.
translations.idiomatic: Qi is distant and our bond thin—better to bind their envoy and send him to the capital, and ask the throne to strike them down.

sentences.zh: 上嘉大夫忠，所請宜許。」

translations.literal: The emperor will praise your lordship's loyalty; what you request should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor will reward your loyalty, and your request will surely be granted.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽寤，使真作奏。

translations.literal: Weiyue awoke to this and had Zhen draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue was persuaded and had Zhen draft a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 震與將吏議不可，惟嶽又從之。

translations.literal: Zhen and the generals and officials debated that it could not be done; Weiyue again followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhen and the officers argued against it, and Weiyue again sided with them.

sentences.zh: 其舅谷從政，豪俊士也，切諫不納。

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Gu Congzheng, a bold and outstanding man, remonstrated urgently but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Gu Congzheng, a man of force and talent, pleaded urgently in vain.

sentences.zh: 於是張孝忠以易州歸天子，天子詔朱滔與孝忠合兵討惟嶽，盡赦吏士，購惟嶽首有賞。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang Xiaozhong submitted Yizhou to the Son of Heaven; the Son of Heaven ordered Zhu Tao and Xiaozhong to unite forces to attack Weiyue, pardoned all officers and soldiers, and offered a reward for Weiyue's head.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaozhong then surrendered Yizhou to the emperor, who ordered Zhu Tao and Xiaozhong to join forces against Weiyue, granted a general amnesty to his followers, and posted a bounty for Weiyue's head.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽與滔戰束鹿，大奔。

translations.literal: Weiyue fought Tao at Shulu and fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue met Tao at Shulu and was routed.

sentences.zh: 遂圍深州。

translations.literal: They then besieged Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armies then laid siege to Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，率兵萬餘，使王武俊爭束鹿，田悅亦遣孟祐來助。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he led more than ten thousand troops, sent Wang Wujun to contest Shulu, and Tian Yue also dispatched Meng You to assist.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year he led over ten thousand men, sent Wang Wujun to recover Shulu, and Tian Yue dispatched Meng You to help.

sentences.zh: 武俊以精兵先陷陣，師卻。

translations.literal: Wujun led elite troops to break the enemy line first; the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun led the crack troops in a frontal assault, but the army was driven back.

sentences.zh: 滔繢帛為狻猊，使壯士百人蒙以噪，趨惟嶽軍，馬駭軍亂，因大敗，火其營去。

translations.literal: Tao embroidered silk into lion shapes, had a hundred stalwarts cover themselves with them and raise a clamor, rushed at Weiyue's army; the horses panicked, the army fell into disorder, and he was greatly defeated and burned the camp as he left.
translations.idiomatic: Tao had silk fashioned into lion masks; a hundred strong men wore them, raised a deafening roar, and charged Weiyue's lines; the horses panicked, the ranks broke, and Weiyue was routed and burned his camp in retreat.

sentences.zh: 於是深州日急，悅亦嬰城矣。

translations.literal: Shenzhou grew daily more desperate, and Yue also shut himself within the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Shenzhou tightened by the day, and Yue too was trapped inside his walls.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽懼，召真議遣使詣河東馬燧，令其弟惟簡見帝，斬大將謝罪，以兵屬鄭詵，身朝京師。

translations.literal: Weiyue was afraid, summoned Zhen to discuss sending an envoy to Hedong to Ma Sui, having his younger brother Weijian see the emperor, beheading a great general to apologize, placing the troops under Zheng Shen, and going himself to court.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Weiyue called Zhen to plan sending envoys to Ma Sui in Hedong, dispatching his brother Weijian to the emperor, executing a senior commander as an apology, handing the army to Zheng Shen, and going to the capital in person.

sentences.zh: 孟祐知其謀，走告悅，悅使扈岌來讓曰：「敝邑暴兵，本為君索命節，豈為叛逆耶？

translations.literal: Meng You learned of the plot, ran to inform Yue; Yue sent Hu Ji to reproach him, saying: "Our humble district raised troops originally to win you the commission for you—how is that rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Meng You discovered the plan and fled to warn Yue, who sent Hu Ji to rebuke Weiyue: "We took up arms only to win you your father's commission—when did we become rebels?

sentences.zh: 雖見破於馬燧，而感激士大夫乘城拒守，以為後圖。

translations.literal: Though broken by Ma Sui, moved by the devotion of the scholar-officials who manned the walls in defense, we hold this for later plans.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ma Sui has beaten us, our gentlemen still hold the walls out of loyalty—we are planning for the long term.

sentences.zh: 今君信邵真讒間，欲歸悅之罪，以自湔蕩，何負而然！

translations.literal: Now you trust Shao Zhen's slander, wish to lay Yue's guilt upon yourself to cleanse yourself—what have we done to deserve this!
translations.idiomatic: Now you heed Shao Zhen's slanders and would shift the blame onto us to clear your own name—what have we done to you!

sentences.zh: 不則遣祐還軍，無遺王師禽。

translations.literal: Otherwise send You back with the army; do not let the imperial troops capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise send Meng You back with his troops—do not leave him to be taken by the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 若能誅真以徇，請事公如初。」

translations.literal: If you can execute Zhen as an example, we ask to serve you as before.
translations.idiomatic: Execute Zhen as a warning, and we will stand with you as before.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽懦不能決，畢華見曰：「大夫與魏盟未久，魏雖被圍，彼多蓄積，未可下。

translations.literal: Weiyue was timid and could not decide; Bi Hua came forward and said: "Your lordship's alliance with Wei is not long; though Wei is besieged, they have great stores and cannot be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue, too weak-willed to decide, heard Bi Hua say, "Your pact with Wei is fresh; though besieged, they have ample stores and will not fall quickly.

sentences.zh: 齊兵勁地廣，裾帶山河，所謂東秦險固之國，與相持維，足以抗天下。

translations.literal: Qi's troops are strong and its territory broad, skirted by mountains and rivers—the so-called secure state of eastern Qin; if you hold each other in balance, it is enough to resist all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's army is fierce and its lands vast, girded by mountains and rivers—the fortress of the east; keep them as your counterweight and you can stand against the empire.

sentences.zh: 夫背義不詳，輕慮生禍。

translations.literal: To betray righteousness is inauspicious; rash thought breeds disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Betrayal brings ill fortune; reckless plans invite ruin.

sentences.zh: 且孟祐驍將，王武俊善戰，前日逐滔，滔僅免，今合兩將，破滔必矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Meng You is a fierce general and Wang Wujun excels in battle; the other day they drove off Tao, and Tao barely escaped; now with the two generals united, Tao will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Meng You is a daring commander and Wang Wujun a superb fighter; they already chased Tao to the brink of capture—unite them again and Tao is finished.

sentences.zh: 惟審圖之！」

translations.literal: Only consider this carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: Think this through carefully!"

sentences.zh: 惟嶽見深圍未解，畏祐還，乃斬真以謝悅。

translations.literal: Weiyue saw the siege of Shenzhou was not lifted, feared You's return, and beheaded Zhen to apologize to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Shenzhou still besieged and fearing Meng You's withdrawal, Weiyue executed Zhen to appease Yue.

sentences.zh: 明日復戰，又大敗。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again and were again greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again the next day and were routed once more.

sentences.zh: 而康日知舉趙州聽命，惟嶽益困，乃付牙將衛常寧兵五千，而俾王武俊騎八百攻日知。

translations.literal: Kang Rizhi meanwhile raised Zhaozhou in submission to orders; Weiyue grew still more distressed, entrusted five thousand troops to the yamen general Wei Changning, and sent Wang Wujun with eight hundred horsemen to attack Rizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Rizhi had meanwhile submitted Zhaozhou to the court; increasingly desperate, Weiyue gave five thousand men to Wei Changning and sent Wang Wujun with eight hundred cavalry against Rizhi.

sentences.zh: 武俊才雄，素為惟嶽忌，及師行，謂常寧曰：「大夫信讒，吾朝不圖晏，是行勝與否，吾不復入恒矣！

translations.literal: Wujun was talented and bold and had long been envied by Weiyue; as the army marched he said to Changning: "The lord believes slander; I did not expect to see evening at court—whether this campaign wins or loses, I will not enter Heng again!
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was gifted and fierce and had long been distrusted by Weiyue; on the march he told Changning, "Our master heeds slander—I never expected to live to see another peaceful day at court. Win or lose this campaign, I will not return to Hengzhou!

sentences.zh: 將以身托定州張公，安能持頸就刀乎？」

translations.literal: I will entrust myself to Lord Zhang of Dingzhou—how could I stretch out my neck to the blade?
translations.idiomatic: I will throw in my lot with Zhang of Dingzhou—why should I offer my neck to the executioner's knife?

sentences.zh: 常寧與副李獻誠曰：「君不聞詔書乎？

translations.literal: Changning and the deputy Li Xiancheng said: "Have you not heard the imperial edict?
translations.idiomatic: Changning and his deputy Li Xiancheng replied, "Have you not heard the emperor's proclamation?

sentences.zh: 斬大夫首以其官畀之。

translations.literal: Behead the lord and give his office to the one who does it.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever takes the lord's head will receive his post.

sentences.zh: 觀大夫勢終為滔滅，若倒戈還府，事實易圖，有如不捷，張公可歸也。」

translations.literal: Seeing that the lord's position will in the end be destroyed by Tao, if you turn your spears and return to the headquarters the matter is in truth easy to accomplish; if it does not succeed, you can still go over to Lord Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: The lord is doomed to fall to Zhu Tao; turn your troops homeward and the deed is simple—and if it fails, you can still throw in with Zhang of Dingzhou."

sentences.zh: 武俊然之。

translations.literal: Wujun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun assented.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽使要藉官謝遵至武俊壁議事，武俊與謀，使內應。

translations.literal: Weiyue sent the yamen guest officer Xie Zun to Wujun's camp to discuss affairs; Wujun plotted with him and arranged an inside response.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue dispatched the staff officer Xie Zun to Wujun's camp for talks; Wujun conspired with him and set up men within the city.

sentences.zh: 至期，啟城門，武俊入，殺人廷中，無亢者。

translations.literal: When the day came they opened the city gate; Wujun entered and killed men in the court; none resisted.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed time the gates opened; Wujun entered, struck down those in the courtyard, and met no resistance.

sentences.zh: 乃傳令曰：「大夫叛命，今且取之，敢拒者族！」

translations.literal: He then proclaimed: "The lord has rebelled against orders; we now take him—whoever dares resist, his clan will be destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: He issued orders: "The lord has defied the throne—we seize him now; resist and your whole clan dies!

sentences.zh: 士不敢動。

translations.literal: The soldiers did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: The troops dared not stir.

sentences.zh: 武俊使裨校任越牽惟嶽出，縊之戟門下，並殺鄭詵、他奴等數十人，使子士真傳首京師。

translations.literal: Wujun had his lieutenant Ren Yue drag Weiyue out, strangled him beneath the halberd gate, and together killed Zheng Shen, Tanu, and several tens of others; he sent his son Shizhen to deliver the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun had his officer Ren Yue haul Weiyue out and hang him beneath the halberd gate, executed Zheng Shen, Tanu, and dozens more, and sent his son Shizhen to present the head at court.

sentences.zh: 帝盡赦其府將士，給部中租役三年。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned all the headquarters generals and soldiers and granted three years' exemption from rents and corvée in the district.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted a full amnesty to the garrison and exempted the region from taxes and labor levies for three years.

sentences.zh: 真始事寶臣，掌文記，武俊表其忠，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Zhen had first served Baochen, managing documents; Wujun memorialized his loyalty and he was posthumously made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had served Baochen as chief secretary; Wujun praised his loyalty, and the court posthumously appointed him Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 其息呂擢冀州長史。

translations.literal: His son Lü was promoted to chief administrator of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lü was appointed chief administrator of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 常寧在武俊時用事，為內史監，其後謀亂，誅。

translations.literal: Changning wielded power under Wujun as Director of the Palace Secretariat; later he plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Changning held sway under Wujun as Director of the Palace Secretariat; he later plotted revolt and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽異母兄惟誠，尚儒術，謙裕，寶臣愛之，使決軍事，以惟嶽正嫡，固讓不肯當。

translations.literal: Weiyue's half-brother Weicheng esteemed Confucian learning, was modest and generous; Baochen loved him and had him decide military affairs, but because Weiyue was the legitimate heir he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue's half-brother Weicheng was devoted to the classics, modest and open-handed; Baochen favored him and entrusted him with military decisions, but as Weiyue was the legitimate heir Weicheng steadfastly refused the role.

sentences.zh: 其妹妻李納，故寶臣請惟誠復故姓，而仕諸鄆，為納營田副使，四為州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger sister was married to Li Na; therefore Baochen asked Weicheng to resume his original surname, and he served in Yanzhou as Na's deputy commissioner of agricultural colonies, four times as a prefectural governor.
translations.idiomatic: His sister was married to Li Na, so Baochen had Weicheng take back his birth surname; he served in Yanzhou as Na's deputy for military colonies and held four prefectural governorships.

sentences.zh: 初，惟嶽叛，弟惟簡以家僮票士百餘奉母鄭奔京師，帝拘於客省。

translations.literal: At first, when Weiyue rebelled, his younger brother Weijian took more than a hundred household retainers and brave men to escort their mother Lady Zheng to the capital; the emperor detained them in the guest quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiyue rebelled, his brother Weijian fled to the capital with over a hundred household guards escorting their mother Lady Zheng; the emperor held them in the guest residence.

sentences.zh: 及出奉天，惟簡將赴難，謀於鄭，鄭曰：「爾父立功河朔，位宰相，身未嘗至京師，兄死於人手。

translations.literal: When they set out for Fengtian, Weijian was about to go to the rescue and consulted Lady Zheng; Zheng said: "Your father achieved merit north of the Yellow River, rose to chancellor, yet never came to the capital in person; your elder brother died by another's hand.
translations.idiomatic: As the court withdrew to Fengtian, Weijian prepared to join the fight and sought his mother's counsel; Lady Zheng said, "Your father won glory on the northern frontier and rose to chancellor, yet never set foot in the capital; your brother died at another's hands.

sentences.zh: 爾入朝，未識天子，不能效忠，吾不子汝矣！」

translations.literal: You have entered court, do not know the Son of Heaven, and cannot show loyalty—I will no longer call you my son!
translations.idiomatic: You have come to court without ever knowing the emperor—if you cannot prove your loyalty, you are no son of mine!

sentences.zh: 督其行曰：「而能死王事，吾不朽矣！」

translations.literal: She urged him on, saying: "If you can die in the king's service, I shall not perish!"
translations.idiomatic: She pressed him: "Die in the emperor's service, and I shall live on in you!"

sentences.zh: 乃斬關出，道更七戰，得及行在。

translations.literal: He then cut through the passes and went out, fought seven more battles on the road, and reached the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: He fought his way through the passes, won seven engagements on the road, and reached the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 帝見厚撫之，拜太子諭德，討賊有功。

translations.literal: The emperor received him, treated him generously, appointed him Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and he had merit in punishing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed him warmly, named him Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and he distinguished himself against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 帝徙山南，惟簡以三十騎從，夜失道，馳至盩厔西，聞中人語，問天子所在，密語曰：「上在此。」

translations.literal: When the emperor moved into the southern mountains, Weijian followed with thirty horsemen; at night they lost the way, galloped to the west of Zhouzhi, heard eunuchs speaking, asked where the Son of Heaven was, and was told in secret: "His Majesty is here.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew into the southern mountains, Weijian followed with thirty horsemen; they lost their way at night, rode west of Zhouzhi, overheard eunuchs, asked where the emperor was, and was whispered, "His Majesty is here.

sentences.zh: 帝見之流涕，執其手曰：「爾有母，乃能從朕耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor saw him and wept, took his hand and said: "You have a mother—yet you could follow me?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept at the sight of him, clasped his hand, and said, "You have a mother—yet you came with me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣誓以死！」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant vows to die!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I pledge my life to Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 比明，北方有塵起，帝憂。

translations.literal: By dawn dust rose in the north; the emperor was worried.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak dust appeared to the north, and the emperor grew anxious.

sentences.zh: 惟簡登高曰：「渾瑊以騎來。」

translations.literal: Weijian climbed high and said: "Hun Jian is coming with cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Weijian climbed a height and called, "It is Hun Jian's cavalry.

sentences.zh: 瑊至，遂決趨興元，惟簡前導。

translations.literal: When Jian arrived, they resolved to hurry to Xingyuan; Weijian went ahead as guide.
translations.idiomatic: Jian arrived, and they set out for Xingyuan with Weijian leading the way.

sentences.zh: 及帝還，封武安郡王，號元從功臣，圖形淩煙閣，賜鐵券。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu'an, titled an original companion meritorious subject, his portrait placed in the Lingyan Pavilion, and granted an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Weijian was created Prince of Wu'an, hailed as a founding companion of merit, his portrait hung in the Lingyan Pavilion, and given an iron certificate of immunity.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，為左金吾衛大將軍，長史萬國俊奪興平民田，吏畏不敢治，至是訴於惟簡，即日廢國俊，以地與民。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's time he was Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard; the chief administrator Wan Guojun seized farmland of the common people of Xingping; officials feared him and dared not prosecute; they then appealed to Weijian, who the same day dismissed Guojun and returned the land to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzong he served as Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard; the chief administrator Wan Guojun seized farmland from Xingping peasants, and officials dared not act until the case reached Weijian, who dismissed Guojun that same day and restored the land.

sentences.zh: 出為鳳翔節度使，市耕牛佃具給農，歲增墾數十萬畝。

translations.literal: Sent out as military commissioner of Fengxiang, he purchased plow oxen and tenant tools to supply the farmers, and each year added several hundred thousand mu of reclaimed land.
translations.idiomatic: As military commissioner of Fengxiang he bought oxen and farm implements for the peasants, adding several hundred thousand mu of newly opened fields each year.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十五，贈尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-five, and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-five and was posthumously appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子元本，輕薄無行。

translations.literal: His son Yuanben was frivolous and without proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanben was dissolute and ill-behaved.

sentences.zh: 長慶末，與薛渾私侍襄陽公主，事敗，主幽禁中，元本以功臣子，貸死，流嶺南。

translations.literal: At the end of Changqing he privately attended Princess Xiangyang with Xue Hun; the affair was exposed, the princess was confined in the palace, and Yuanben, as a meritorious subject's son, was spared death but exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Changqing era he had a secret affair with Princess Xiangyang alongside Xue Hun; when it was exposed the princess was imprisoned, and Yuanben, as a meritorious subject's son, was spared execution but banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 弟銖，好學多識，有儒者風。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhu loved learning and was widely informed, with the air of a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhu was studious and erudite, with the bearing of a scholar.

sentences.zh: 王武俊字元英，本出契丹怒皆部。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun, style name Yuanying, was originally from the Khitan Nujie tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun, courtesy name Yuanying, was originally of the Khitan Nujie tribe.

sentences.zh: 父路俱，開元中，與饒樂府都督李詩等五千帳求襲冠帶，入居薊。

translations.literal: His father Luju, in the Kaiyuan era, with the Raole prefecture commissioner Li Shi and five thousand households sought to receive caps and belts, and entered to settle in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luju, in the Kaiyuan reign, joined Raole commissioner Li Shi and five thousand households in petitioning for Chinese titles and settled in Ji.

sentences.zh: 武俊甫十五，善騎射，與張孝忠齊名，隸李寶臣帳下為裨將。

translations.literal: Wujun was only fifteen, excelled at mounted archery, was famed equally with Zhang Xiaozhong, and served under Li Baochen's banner as a lieutenant.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Wujun was already renowned for horsemanship and archery, ranked with Zhang Xiaozhong, and served Li Baochen as a deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，王師入井陘，武俊謂寶臣曰：「以寡敵眾，曲遇直，戰則離，守則潰，銳師遠鬥，庸可禦乎！」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying the imperial army entered Jingxing; Wujun said to Baochen: "With few against many, a crooked line meeting a straight one—fight and they scatter, hold and they collapse; crack troops fighting far from home—how can they be withstood!
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoying era the imperial army entered Jingxing Pass; Wujun told Baochen, "Few against many, a bent line against a straight one—they fight and break apart, they hold and they crumble; elite troops fighting far from home—how can they stand?

sentences.zh: 寶臣遂以恒、定等五州自歸，共平餘賊，武俊謀也。

translations.literal: Baochen then submitted the five prefectures of Heng, Ding, and others of his own accord, and together they pacified the remaining rebels—this was Wujun's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen then surrendered the five prefectures including Heng and Ding and helped crush the remaining rebels—Wujun's counsel made it possible.

sentences.zh: 奏兼御史中丞，封維川郡王。

translations.literal: He was memorialized as concurrently Censor-in-Chief and enfeoffed as Prince of Weichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed concurrent Censor-in-Chief and created Prince of Weichuan.

sentences.zh: 其子士真，亦沈悍有斷，寶臣倚愛，出入帳中，以女妻之。

translations.literal: His son Shizhen was also deep, fierce, and decisive; Baochen relied on and loved him, he went in and out of the tent, and Baochen gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizhen was likewise resolute and fierce; Baochen favored him, kept him at his side, and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 寶臣以疑殺許崇俊等，士真密結左右，故武俊免於難。

translations.literal: Baochen killed Xu Chongjun and others out of suspicion; Shizhen secretly won over those around him, and so Wujun escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Baochen executed Xu Chongjun and others on suspicion, Shizhen quietly secured allies in the camp, and Wujun survived.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽拒命，或言武俊有他誌，武俊知之，出入導從才一二，未嘗接賓客。

translations.literal: When Weiyue defied orders, some said Wujun had other designs; Wujun knew this, and when he went out had only one or two attendants, never receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiyue rebelled, some whispered that Wujun harbored other ambitions; aware of this, he went abroad with only one or two attendants and received no guests.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽雖內疑，然見其屈損，又惜善鬥，末忍殺。

translations.literal: Though Weiyue inwardly suspected him, he saw him humbled and also valued his skill in battle, and in the end could not bear to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue suspected him inwardly, yet saw him humbled and prized his fighting skill, and in the end could not bring himself to kill him.

sentences.zh: 康日知以趙州降，惟嶽謀伐之，皆曰：「武俊故心膂，先君命之使佐大夫，而士真又大夫女弟婿，今事急，宜去猜嫌以任之，不然，尚誰使？」

translations.literal: Kang Rizhi submitted Zhaozhou; Weiyue planned to attack him; all said: "Wujun was your father's trusted core; the late lord ordered him to assist you, and Shizhen is moreover your wife's brother-in-law; now affairs are urgent—you should drop suspicion and employ him; otherwise, whom else can you use?
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Rizhi surrendered Zhaozhou, Weiyue planned an attack; his advisers said, "Wujun was your father's right hand; Shizhen is your sister's husband—drop your suspicions and trust him now, or whom else can you send?

sentences.zh: 乃遣與衛常寧將兵往。

translations.literal: He then sent him with Wei Changning to lead troops there.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Wujun with Wei Changning at the head of the army.

sentences.zh: 因謀執惟嶽，而日知亦遣人邀說以禍福，武俊乃還兵，使人謂惟嶽曰：「大夫與齊、魏同惡，今魏兵已敗，齊為趙州所限，幽州兵近在定，三軍且救死。

translations.literal: They then plotted to seize Weiyue; Rizhi also sent someone to invite persuasion by fortune and disaster; Wujun turned the army back and sent someone to tell Weiyue: "You, my lord, share guilt with Qi and Wei; now Wei's army is defeated, Qi is constrained by Zhaozhou, Youzhou troops are near at Ding—the three armies are about to fight for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted to seize Weiyue while Rizhi also sent envoys promising reward or ruin; Wujun turned back and warned Weiyue, "You stand with Qi and Wei; Wei's army is broken, Qi is pinned by Zhaozhou, and Youzhou troops are at Dingzhou—all three armies are fighting for survival.

sentences.zh: 聞有詔召大夫，宜亟歸。」

translations.literal: We hear there is an edict summoning you, my lord—you should hurry back.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial summons is on its way—you should return at once.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽惶遽出，遂縊。

translations.literal: Weiyue fled in panic and was strangled.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue fled in panic and was hanged.

sentences.zh: 即遣其屬孟華奏天子。

translations.literal: He at once sent his subordinate Meng Hua to memorialize the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent Meng Hua to report to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 華辯對稱旨，德宗擢為兵部郎中，授武俊檢校秘書監兼御史大夫、恒冀觀察使。

translations.literal: Hua's eloquent replies pleased the emperor; Dezong promoted him to Director in the Ministry of War and appointed Wujun Acting Director of the Palace Library, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and Commissioner for the Heng-Ji Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Hua's replies pleased Emperor Dezong, who promoted him to a post in the Ministry of War and appointed Wujun Acting Director of the Palace Library and Censor-in-Chief, with charge of the Heng-Ji circuit.

sentences.zh: 是時，惟嶽將楊政義以定降，楊榮國以深降，朱滔受而戍之。

translations.literal: At that time Weiyue's generals Yang Zhengyi submitted Ding, Yang Rongguo submitted Shen, and Zhu Tao accepted them and garrisoned the places.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue's generals Yang Zhengyi surrendered Dingzhou and Yang Rongguo surrendered Shenzhou; Zhu Tao accepted both and stationed troops there.

sentences.zh: 帝以定賜張孝忠，而日知為深趙觀察使。

translations.literal: The emperor gave Ding to Zhang Xiaozhong and made Rizhi Commissioner for the Shen-Zhao Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Dingzhou to Zhang Xiaozhong and made Rizhi commissioner of the Shen-Zhao circuit.

sentences.zh: 武俊怨不得節度而失趙、定，滔亦怨失深州，二人相結。

translations.literal: Wujun resented not receiving the commissionership and losing Zhao and Ding; Tao also resented losing Shenzhou; the two joined forces.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun resented being denied the commissionership and losing Zhao and Ding; Tao resented the loss of Shenzhou; the two allied.

sentences.zh: 武俊即縛使者送滔，與之叛。

translations.literal: Wujun at once bound the envoy and sent him to Tao, and rebelled with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun seized the imperial envoy, sent him to Tao, and joined the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，詔華諭解，不聽。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he ordered Hua to persuade and explain; Wujun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Hua to reason with him, but Wujun refused.

sentences.zh: 時馬燧、李抱真、李芃、李晟討田悅，悅方困，武俊、滔救之，屯連篋山。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Sui, Li Baozhen, Li Qi, and Li Sheng were attacking Tian Yue; Yue was in distress; Wujun and Tao rescued him and encamped linked at Qieshan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui, Li Baozhen, Li Qi, and Li Sheng were besieging Tian Yue when Wujun and Tao came to his relief and camped together at Qieshan.

sentences.zh: 帝詔李懷光督神策兵助討賊，軍就舍，氣銳甚，謂燧曰：「奉詔毋養寇，及壁壘未成擊之，可滅也。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Li Huai'guang to lead the Shence army to help attack the rebels; when the army reached camp their spirit was very sharp; he said to Sui: "By edict we must not nurture bandits—strike before their ramparts are finished and they can be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li Huai'guang and the Shence army to join the campaign; arriving in high spirits, he told Sui, "Our orders are not to let the rebels grow—strike before their walls are complete and we can finish them.

sentences.zh: 乃縱兵入滔壁，殺千餘人。

translations.literal: He then loosed his troops into Tao's ramparts and killed more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He charged into Tao's camp and killed over a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 悅軍既屢北，不能陣。

translations.literal: Yue's army, having repeatedly been defeated, could not form battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's army, beaten again and again, could not hold formation.

sentences.zh: 懷光緩轡觀之，武俊乘其怠，使趙萬敵等以二千騎橫突，而滔軍踵馳，王師亂，相蹈藉死，屍梗河為不流。

translations.literal: Huai'guang slowed his reins to watch; Wujun seized their slackness and had Zhao Wandi and others with two thousand horsemen charge across; Tao's army followed at the gallop; the imperial army fell into disorder, trampling one another to death; corpses choked the river so it would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang reined in to watch the field; Wujun struck at the moment of slackness, sending Zhao Wandi with two thousand horsemen in a flanking charge while Tao's troops thundered after; the imperial army broke, men trampled one another to death, and corpses dammed the river.

sentences.zh: 懷光還走壁。

translations.literal: Huai'guang turned back and ran to his ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang fled back to his camp.

sentences.zh: 武俊夜決河註王莽渠，斷燧餉路。

translations.literal: Wujun by night diverted the river into the Wang Mang Canal and cut off Sui's supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun diverted the river by night into the Wang Mang Canal and severed Sui's supply line.

sentences.zh: 燧計窮，而與滔素姻家，乃遣使謾謝滔曰：「老夫不自量，與諸君遇。

translations.literal: Sui's plans were exhausted; he was moreover old affines with Tao, and sent an envoy falsely apologizing to Tao, saying: "This old man did not measure himself before meeting you all.
translations.idiomatic: At his wits' end, and being related to Tao by marriage, Sui sent an envoy with a feigned apology: "I underestimated you all.

sentences.zh: 王大夫善戰，天下無前，吾固宜敗，幸公圖之，使老夫得還河東，諸將亦罷兵，吾為言天子，以河北地付公。」

translations.literal: Lord Wang excels in battle, unmatched under heaven; I ought indeed to be defeated; pray arrange matters so this old man can return to Hedong, the generals also cease arms, and I will speak to the Son of Heaven to entrust the Hebei lands to you.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Wang fights as none under heaven; I deserve defeat. Help me withdraw to Hedong, disband the armies, and I will ask the emperor to give you all of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 滔亦陰忌武俊勝且不制，即謂武俊曰：「王師既敗，馬公卑約如此，不宜迫人以險。」

translations.literal: Tao also secretly feared that if Wujun won he could not control him, and said to Wujun: "The imperial army is already defeated; Lord Ma's humble terms are such—you should not drive men to extremity."
translations.idiomatic: Tao secretly feared Wujun's victory would leave him uncontrollable and urged, "The imperial army is beaten and Ma Sui begs so humbly—do not drive him to desperation."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「燧等皆國名臣，連兵十萬，一戰而北，貽羞國家，不知何面目見天子耶？

translations.literal: He replied: "Sui and the rest are famed ministers of the state; they linked a hundred thousand troops and were routed in one battle—bringing shame on the nation; what face have they to see the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Wujun answered, "Sui and his colleagues are the empire's great ministers; they brought a hundred thousand men and fled in one battle—how can they face the emperor?

sentences.zh: 彼行不五十里，必反拒我。」

translations.literal: They will not march fifty li before they turn back to resist us."
translations.idiomatic: They will not go fifty li before they turn and fight us again."

sentences.zh: 滔固許之。

translations.literal: Tao firmly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Tao agreed.

sentences.zh: 燧至魏縣，堅壁自固，師復振。

translations.literal: Sui reached Weixian, held his walls firmly, and the army's spirit revived.
translations.idiomatic: Sui reached Weixian, fortified his camp, and his army rallied.

sentences.zh: 滔慚謝，嫌隙始構矣。

translations.literal: Tao apologized in shame, and enmity began to form between them.
translations.idiomatic: Tao apologized in embarrassment, and rift between them began to grow.

sentences.zh: 武俊使張鐘葵攻趙州，日知斬其首以聞。

translations.literal: Wujun sent Zhang Zhongkui to attack Zhaozhou; Rizhi beheaded him and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun sent Zhang Zhongkui against Zhaozhou; Rizhi killed him and sent his head to court.

sentences.zh: 於是武俊與田悅等擅相王。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wujun and Tian Yue and others on their own authority made one another kings.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun, Tian Yue, and the others then proclaimed one another kings without imperial sanction.

sentences.zh: 武俊國號趙，以恒為真定府，命士真留守兼元帥；

translations.literal: Wujun's state was named Zhao; he made Heng the Zhending prefecture and ordered Shizhen to remain on guard as concurrent commander-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: Wujun named his realm Zhao, made Heng the seat of Zhending prefecture, and left Shizhen as garrison commander and supreme marshal;

sentences.zh: 以畢華、鄭儒為左右內史，王士良司刑，王佑司文，士清司武，並為尚書；

translations.literal: he made Bi Hua and Zheng Ru Left and Right Palace Secretaries, Wang Shiliang Director of Punishments, Wang You Director of Documents, Shiqing Director of War—all as Ministers;
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Bi Hua and Zheng Ru as Left and Right Palace Secretaries, Wang Shiliang as Director of Punishments, Wang You as Director of Documents, and Shiqing as Director of War, all with ministerial rank;

sentences.zh: 士則司文侍郎，宋端給事中，王洽內史舍人，張士清執憲大夫，衛常寧內史監，皇甫祝尚書右仆射，餘以次封拜。

translations.literal: Shize as Vice Director of Documents, Song Duan as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Wang Qia as Secretariat Attendant, Zhang Shiqing as Censor-in-Chief, Wei Changning as Director of the Palace Secretariat, Huangfu Zhu as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs—the rest enfeoffed and appointed in order.
translations.idiomatic: Shize became Vice Director of Documents, Song Duan Attendant-in-Ordinary, Wang Qia Secretariat Attendant, Zhang Shiqing Censor-in-Chief, Wei Changning Director of the Palace Secretariat, Huangfu Zhu Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and the rest were enfeoffed and promoted in turn.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，抱真使客賈林詐降武俊，既見，曰：「吾來傳詔，非降也。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, Baozhen sent his retainer Jia Lin to feign surrender to Wujun; once he saw him he said: "I have come to transmit an edict, not to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, Baozhen sent his agent Jia Lin to Wujun under pretense of surrender; when they met, Lin said, "I bring an imperial message—I am not here to submit.

sentences.zh: 武俊色動，林曰：「天子知大夫登壇建國撫膺顧左右曰：『我本忠義，天子不省，故至是。』

translations.literal: Wujun's expression changed; Lin said: "The Son of Heaven knows that when you, my lord, ascended the altar and founded a state you beat your breast and looked to those beside you, saying: 'I was originally loyal and righteous; the Son of Heaven did not understand, and so it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun's face changed; Lin said, "The emperor knows that when you took the throne you struck your breast and told your attendants, 'I was always loyal; the emperor would not see it, and so I came to this.

sentences.zh: 今諸軍數表大夫至誠，上見表動色曰：『朕前誤無及矣。

translations.literal: Now the armies have repeatedly memorialized your lordship's utmost sincerity; when the emperor saw the memorials his expression changed and he said: 'My earlier mistake cannot be undone.
translations.idiomatic: The armies have repeatedly testified to your loyalty; reading their memorials, the emperor said with emotion, 'My earlier error cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 朋友失意尚可謝，朕四海主，毫芒過失，返不得自新耶！』

translations.literal: If a friend is disappointed one can still apologize; I am lord of the four seas—can I not renew myself over the slightest fault!
translations.idiomatic: A friend may be reconciled after a quarrel—am I, lord of the four seas, unable to mend the smallest fault?

sentences.zh: 今大夫親斷逆首，而宰相阇於事宜，國家與大夫烏有細故哉？

translations.literal: Now you, my lord, personally cut off the rebel head, yet the chancellors are blind to the situation—what petty matter stands between the state and you?
translations.idiomatic: You yourself slew the rebel leader, yet the chancellors misunderstand the times—what petty quarrel can stand between you and the throne?

sentences.zh: 朱滔以利相動，公何取焉？

translations.literal: Zhu Tao moves you with profit—what do you gain from him?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao tempts you with gain—what do you gain by following him?

sentences.zh: 誠能與昭義同心，曠然改圖，上不失君臣之義，下以為子孫計。」

translations.literal: If you can truly join Zhaoyi in one mind, openly change your plan, above you will not lose the righteousness of ruler and subject, below you will plan for your descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Stand with Zhaoyi in unity, change course openly, keep faith with the throne above, and secure your heirs below."

sentences.zh: 武俊曰：「仆虜人也，尚知撫百姓，天子固不務殺人以安天下。

translations.literal: Wujun said: "I am a barbarian slave, yet I still know to cherish the common people; the Son of Heaven surely does not seek to pacify the world by killing.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun said, "I am a barbarian, yet even I know to care for the people; the emperor surely does not mean to pacify the realm by slaughter.

sentences.zh: 今山東連兵比戰，骨盡暴野，雖勝尚誰與居？

translations.literal: Now east of the mountains armies fight in succession; bones lie exposed across the fields—even if we win, with whom shall we dwell?
translations.idiomatic: Armies east of the mountains fight without end; bones litter the fields—even victory leaves no one to enjoy it.

sentences.zh: 今不憚歸國，業與諸軍盟，虜性樸強，不欲曲在我，天子若能以恩蕩刷之，我首倡歸命，有不從者，奉辭伐之，河北不五十日可定。」

translations.literal: I do not now shrink from returning to the state; I have already allied with the armies; barbarian nature is plain and stubborn—I do not wish the wrong to be on my side; if the Son of Heaven can wash it away with grace, I will be first to submit; whoever does not follow, I will take imperial orders to attack; Hebei can be settled in less than fifty days."
translations.idiomatic: I am ready to return to allegiance; I am already allied with the other armies; we barbarians are plain and stubborn and do not want to be in the wrong; if the emperor will cleanse us with mercy, I will lead the way back; whoever refuses, I will march against under imperial orders—and Hebei can be pacified in fifty days."

sentences.zh: 會帝出奉天，抱真將還澤潞，悅說武俊、滔踵襲之。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor went out to Fengtian; Baozhen was about to return to Zelu; Yue persuaded Wujun and Tao to follow and strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the emperor withdrew to Fengtian; as Baozhen prepared to return to Zelu, Yue urged Wujun and Tao to pursue and attack him.

sentences.zh: 林曰：「夫退軍，前輜重，後銳師，人心固壹，不可圖也。

translations.literal: Lin said: "In a withdrawing army, baggage trains are in front and crack troops behind; hearts are firmly united—it cannot be plotted against.
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "A retreating army puts its baggage ahead and its crack troops behind; the men are of one mind—you cannot ambush it.

sentences.zh: 使戰勝得地，利歸於魏，不幸喪師，趙受其災。

translations.literal: If you fight and win and gain land, the benefit goes to Wei; if unluckily you lose the army, Zhao suffers the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: If you win, Wei gains the land; if you lose, Zhao bears the ruin.

sentences.zh: 今滄、趙乃故地，故不取之？」

translations.literal: Now Cang and Zhao are your former lands—will you not take them instead?
translations.idiomatic: Cangzhou and Zhao are your old territories—why not take them instead?

sentences.zh: 武俊遂引而北，林復激之曰：「公異邦豪英，不應謀中夏。

translations.literal: Wujun then led his forces north; Lin again stirred him, saying: "You are a heroic champion of another land—you should not plot against the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun marched north; Lin pressed him again: "You are a hero from beyond—why plot against the heartland?

sentences.zh: 燕、魏幽險，彼王室強則須公之援，削則己欲並吞。

translations.literal: Yan and Wei are deep and perilous; when the royal house is strong they need your aid, when weakened they wish to swallow you themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Wei are rugged strongholds; when the throne is strong they need you, when it weakens they will devour you.

sentences.zh: 且河北惟有趙、魏、燕耳，滔乃稱冀，心圖公冀州矣。

translations.literal: Moreover in Hebei there are only Zhao, Wei, and Yan; Tao has styled himself Ji—his heart is set on your Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei holds only Zhao, Wei, and Yan; Tao has taken the title of Ji—he covets your Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 使滔能制山東，大夫當臣事之，否則見攻。

translations.literal: If Tao can control the east of the mountains, you, my lord, must serve him as subject; otherwise you will be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: If Tao masters the east, you must bow to him—or he will attack you.

sentences.zh: 能臣滔乎？」

translations.literal: Can you serve Tao as subject?"
translations.idiomatic: Could you submit to Tao?"

sentences.zh: 武俊投袂曰：「二百年天子猶不能事，安能臣豎子耶！」

translations.literal: Wujun flung his sleeve and said: "A Son of Heaven of two hundred years I still will not serve—how could I be subject to a stripling!"
translations.idiomatic: Wujun flung aside his sleeve and cried, "I will not serve an emperor of two hundred years—how could I bow to that whelp!"

sentences.zh: 乃定計通好抱真，而約馬燧盟。

translations.literal: He then fixed a plan to open friendly relations with Baozhen and also pledged alliance with Ma Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He resolved to ally with Baozhen and pledged friendship with Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 是時，滔悉幽、薊兵與回紇圍貝州，將絕白馬津，南趨洛，李懷光據河中，李希烈陷汴，南略江淮，李納方叛，唯李晟軍渭上。

translations.literal: At that time Tao mustered the You and Ji armies with the Uyghurs to besiege Beizhou, was about to cut the Baima Ford and march south toward Luoyang; Li Huai'guang held Hezhong, Li Xilie took Bian, raided south toward Jiang and Huai; Li Na had just rebelled; only Li Sheng's army was on the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Tao had massed the You and Ji armies with Uyghur allies against Beizhou, threatened the Baima crossing, and aimed south for Luoyang; Li Huai'guang held Hezhong, Li Xilie had taken Bian and swept toward the Jiang-Huai, Li Na had just rebelled, and only Li Sheng remained on the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 羽書調發天下十之三，人心惴恐。

translations.literal: Dispatch orders flew; a third of all under heaven was mobilized; hearts were fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilization orders raced across the realm; a third of the empire was called to arms, and the people lived in dread.

sentences.zh: 及田緒殺悅，林復說武俊曰：「滔素欲得魏博，會悅死，魏人氣，公不救，魏且下。

translations.literal: When Tian Xu killed Yue, Lin again persuaded Wujun, saying: "Tao has long wanted to gain Weibo; now that Yue is dead the Wei men are dispirited—if you do not rescue them, Wei will fall.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Xu killed Yue, Lin urged Wujun again: "Tao has long coveted Weibo; with Yue dead the Wei troops are demoralized—if you do not save them, Wei will fall.

sentences.zh: 滔益甲數萬，張孝忠將北面事滔，三道連衡，濟以回紇，長驅而南，昭義軍必保山西，則河朔舉入滔矣。

translations.literal: Tao has added tens of thousands of armored troops; Zhang Xiaozhong is about to turn north and serve Tao; three routes link in alliance, aided by the Uyghurs, driving south at length—the Zhaoyi army will surely hold Shanxi, and then all Hebei will enter Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Tao has raised tens of thousands more troops; Zhang Xiaozhong is ready to submit to him from the north; three allied columns, backed by the Uyghurs, will drive south—the Zhaoyi army will hold Shanxi, and all Hebei will fall to Tao.

sentences.zh: 今魏尚完，孝忠未附，公與昭義合兵破之，聲振關中，京邑可坐復，天子反正，不朽之業，誰與公參！」

translations.literal: Now Wei is still intact and Xiaozhong has not yet submitted; if you and Zhaoyi combine armies to defeat him, renown will shake Guanzhong, the capital can be recovered without stir, the Son of Heaven restored to right rule—an immortal achievement; who could share it with you!
translations.idiomatic: Weibo still holds together and Xiaozhong has not gone over to Tao; join Zhaoyi, crush him, and your fame will thunder through Guanzhong. The capital can be retaken from your seat, the emperor restored—and for such an undying feat, who but you could claim a share?

sentences.zh: 武俊大喜，與抱真相聞，自將屯南宮，抱真屯經城，兩軍相距十里而舍。

translations.literal: Wujun was greatly pleased; he exchanged messages with Baozhen, personally led troops to encamp at Nangong, Baozhen encamped at Jingcheng, and the two armies halted ten li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was overjoyed. He opened communications with Baozhen, marched to camp at Nangong while Baozhen camped at Jingcheng, their two armies halting ten li apart.

sentences.zh: 武俊潛會抱真於軍，陳說忼慨，抱真亦傾意結納，約為兄弟，遂俱東壁貝州，距城三十里止。

translations.literal: Wujun secretly met Baozhen in camp, spoke with impassioned fervor; Baozhen also opened his heart and received him, they pledged brotherhood, then together went east to blockade Beizhou and halted thirty li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun stole into Baozhen's camp for a secret meeting and spoke with burning conviction; Baozhen responded in full trust and they swore brotherhood. Together they marched east to invest Beizhou, stopping thirty li from the walls.

sentences.zh: 滔欲迎戰，武俊戒士飽食曰：「軍未合，毋妄動！」

translations.literal: Tao wished to give battle; Wujun warned the soldiers to eat their fill, saying: "The armies have not yet joined—do not act rashly!
translations.idiomatic: Tao prepared to meet them in battle. Wujun ordered his men to eat their fill and warned, "The armies have not yet engaged—hold your ground!

sentences.zh: 遣趙琳、趙萬敵兵五百蔽林以待。

translations.literal: He sent Zhao Lin and Zhao Wandu with five hundred troops to conceal themselves in the forest and wait.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Zhao Lin and Zhao Wandu with five hundred men to lie hidden in the woods in ambush.

sentences.zh: 滔使票將馬寔、盧南史陣而西，李少成引回紇翼之。

translations.literal: Tao sent swift generals Ma Shi and Lu Nanshi to array westward; Li Shaocheng led Uyghur forces to flank them.
translations.idiomatic: Tao sent his swift generals Ma Shi and Lu Nanshi to form a battle line facing west, while Li Shaocheng brought Uyghur cavalry to support them on the wing.

sentences.zh: 日中兵接，武俊與子士清引精騎望少成軍，抱真次之，滔馳騎二百出武俊東南，乘高鼓噪。

translations.literal: At midday the armies clashed; Wujun with his son Shiqing led elite cavalry toward Shaocheng's army, Baozhen followed after, and Tao galloped two hundred horsemen out to Wujun's southeast, beating drums and shouting from high ground.
translations.idiomatic: At noon the battle was joined. Wujun and his son Shiqing led crack cavalry straight at Shaocheng's line, with Baozhen close behind. Tao raced two hundred horsemen to high ground southeast of Wujun and raised a thunderous clamor.

sentences.zh: 武俊使步兵決戰，而自以騎當回紇，勒兵避其銳。

translations.literal: Wujun sent infantry to fight the decisive battle, while he himself with cavalry faced the Uyghurs, restraining his troops to avoid their sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun committed his infantry to the main fight while he personally held the Uyghurs at bay with cavalry, holding his line back from their charge.

sentences.zh: 回紇馬怒突而過，未及返，武俊急擊，琳等兵亦出，回紇驚，中斷，遂先奔。

translations.literal: The Uyghur horses furiously charged through; before they could turn back, Wujun struck hard; Lin's troops also emerged; the Uyghurs were alarmed, cut in two, and fled first.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur horses thundered through the line; before they could wheel about, Wujun struck hard. Lin's hidden troops sprang out as well. The Uyghurs, startled and split in two, broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 初，滔兵蹙武俊軍，不能傷，回紇既卻，即欲引還，因囂不能止，軍大奔，滔走還壁。

translations.literal: At first Tao's troops pressed Wujun's army but could not harm it; once the Uyghurs retreated they wished to withdraw, but because of the clamor could not stop; the army fled in great rout and Tao ran back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: At first Tao's men had pressed Wujun's line without breaking it. When the Uyghurs fell back Tao tried to withdraw, but the uproar could not be checked and his army broke in full flight; Tao himself fled to his camp.

sentences.zh: 武俊中流矢，謂抱真曰：「士少衰，盍以騎濟師，巢穴可覆也。」

translations.literal: Wujun was struck by a stray arrow and said to Baozhen: "Morale has slackened slightly—why not use cavalry to aid the army? Their nest can be overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun took an arrow in the fighting and told Baozhen, "The men's spirit has dipped a little—send cavalry to finish this. We can overrun their camp.

sentences.zh: 抱真使來希皓率勁騎薄滔營，盧玄真乘其後，滔懼，引眾去，希皓迫之，武俊邀於隘，滔大敗，免者八千人。

translations.literal: Baozhen sent Lai Xihao to lead strong cavalry to press Tao's camp; Lu Xuanzhen struck from behind; Tao feared and led his forces away; Xihao pursued, Wujun intercepted at a pass; Tao suffered great defeat and only eight thousand escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen sent Lai Xihao with elite cavalry to storm Tao's camp while Lu Xuanzhen hit him from the rear. Tao fled in alarm. Xihao pressed the pursuit and Wujun blocked the pass. Tao was routed; only eight thousand men got away.

sentences.zh: 會夜，各按屯，武俊營滔東北，抱真營西北。

translations.literal: Night fell; each side rested at camp—Wujun's to Tao's northeast, Baozhen's to the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Night came and both sides encamped—Wujun to Tao's northeast, Baozhen to his northwest.

sentences.zh: 滔知不支，夜半焚車糧，遁歸幽州，火如晝，師大噪，其聲殷地。

translations.literal: Tao knew he could not hold; at midnight he burned carts and grain and fled back to Youzhou; the fire was like daylight; the army raised a great clamor and the sound shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not hold, Tao burned his wagons and stores at midnight and fled toward Youzhou. The blaze lit the night like day; his army roared and the ground trembled with the noise.

sentences.zh: 抱真以山東蝗，食少，歸於潞，武俊亦還。

translations.literal: Baozhen, because of locusts in Shandong and little food, returned to Lu; Wujun also went back.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts had ravaged Shandong and supplies were short, so Baozhen withdrew to Lu. Wujun marched home as well.

sentences.zh: 會有詔復滔官爵，武俊上還幽州盧龍節度。

translations.literal: An edict then restored Tao's offices and ranks; Wujun returned to his post as military governor of Youzhou and Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Tao's titles and offices, and Wujun returned north to resume command of Youzhou and Lulong.

sentences.zh: 又詔以恒州為大都督府，即授武俊長史，賜德、棣二州，以士真為觀察使、清河郡王。

translations.literal: Another edict made Hengzhou a supreme commandery, immediately appointing Wujun chief administrator, granting the two prefectures of De and Di, and making Shizhen observation commissioner and Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict elevated Hengzhou to a supreme commandery, appointed Wujun its chief administrator, granted him De and Di prefectures, and made Shizhen observation commissioner with the title Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 天子至自梁，遇武俊益厚，子弟雖繈褓，悉官之。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned from Liang, he treated Wujun all the more generously; even infants in swaddling clothes among his sons and younger brothers were all given offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Liang, he showered Wujun with favor—even babes still in swaddling clothes among his kin received official appointments.

sentences.zh: 俄進檢校太尉兼中書令，得建廟京師，有司供擬。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Acting Grand Marshal and concurrently Chancellor, permitted to build an ancestral temple in the capital, with the relevant offices providing supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Acting Grand Marshal and Chancellor, granted an ancestral temple in the capital, with the court offices furnishing all provisions.

sentences.zh: 武俊善射，嘗與賓客獵，一日射雞兔九十五，觀者駭伏。

translations.literal: Wujun excelled at archery; once while hunting with guests he shot ninety-five chickens and hares in a single day, and the onlookers were awed and humbled.
