translations.idiomatic: Wujun was a master archer. On one hunt with his guests he brought down ninety-five birds and hares in a single day, leaving the spectators stunned.

sentences.zh: 貞元十七年死，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year of the Zhenyuan era, at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 群臣奉慰天子，如渾瑊故事，贈太師。

translations.literal: The ministers offered condolences to the Son of Heaven following the precedent of Hun Jian, and Wujun was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers offered the emperor condolences on the precedent set at Hun Jian's death, and Wujun was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 有司謚威烈，帝更為忠烈。

translations.literal: The relevant offices proposed the posthumous title Wei Lie; the emperor changed it to Zhong Lie.
translations.idiomatic: The court proposed the posthumous name Wei Lie, "Formidable and Ardent"; the emperor changed it to Zhong Lie, "Loyal and Ardent."

sentences.zh: 士真襲位。

translations.literal: Shizhen succeeded to the position.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen inherited his father's command.

sentences.zh: 士真，其長子也。

translations.literal: Shizhen was his eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen was Wujun's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 少佐父立功，更患難。

translations.literal: In youth he assisted his father in achieving merit and passed through hardships.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had fought at his father's side and shared his trials.

sentences.zh: 既得節度，息兵善守，雖擅置吏，私賦入，而歲貢數十萬緡，比燕、魏為恭。

translations.literal: Once he gained the military governorship he rested the troops and defended well; though he appointed officials on his own authority and collected private levies, he yearly sent tribute of several hundred thousand strings of cash and was more deferential than Yan or Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Once in command he kept the peace and held his ground firmly. Though he appointed his own officials and collected private taxes, he sent the court tribute of hundreds of thousands of strings of cash each year—more obedient in this than the lords of Yan or Wei.

sentences.zh: 元和初，即拜同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was immediately appointed Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanhe era he was appointed a chief minister of state.

sentences.zh: 四年死，贈司徒，謚曰景襄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died; he was posthumously made Minister of Education, with posthumous title Jingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Yuanhe and was posthumously made Minister of Education with the posthumous name Jingxiang.

sentences.zh: 軍中推其子承宗為留後。

translations.literal: The army pushed his son Chengzong as acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: The troops installed his son Chengzong as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 始，河北三鎮自置副大使，常處嫡長，故承宗以御史大夫為之。

translations.literal: At the beginning, the three Hebei circuits each appointed their own deputy commissioners, usually placing the eldest legitimate son in the post; thus Chengzong held it as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: From the start the three Hebei circuits had each appointed their own deputy commissioners, customarily the eldest legitimate son—hence Chengzong had served as Censor-in-Chief in that role.

sentences.zh: 及總留事，憲宗久不報，伺其變。

translations.literal: When he took overall charge as acting commander, Emperor Xianzong long gave no reply, watching for any change.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong assumed full control as acting commander, Emperor Xianzong held back his answer and watched for any sign of defiance.

sentences.zh: 承宗數上疏自言。

translations.literal: Chengzong repeatedly submitted memorials stating his own case.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong sent memorial after memorial pleading his own cause.

sentences.zh: 帝聞劉濟、田季安俱大病，議更建節度。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Liu Ji and Tian Ji'an were both gravely ill and discussed replacing the military governors.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Liu Ji and Tian Ji'an were both seriously ill, the emperor discussed replacing the frontier commanders.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士李絳曰：「鎮州世相繼，人所狃習，惟拒命則討之。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Li Jiang said: "Zhenzhou has passed from father to son for generations; the people are accustomed to it—only if he defies orders should he be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Li Jiang said, "Zhenzhou has been hereditary for generations and the people are used to it. Attack only if Chengzong refuses imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 且諸道之賞饋百萬士，又燕、魏、淄青，勢同必合。

translations.literal: Moreover the various circuits reward and supply a million troops; Yan, Wei, and Ziqing, with the same interest, will surely unite.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the court is already paying to supply a million men across the circuits—and Yan, Wei, and Ziqing share the same interests and will certainly stand together.

sentences.zh: 方江、淮水潦，財力刓困，宜即詔承宗嗣領。

translations.literal: Just now the Jiang and Huai are flooded and finances are exhausted; an edict should immediately install Chengzong as successor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Huai region is under water and the treasury is drained. Confirm Chengzong's succession at once.

sentences.zh: 季安等雖病，徐圖所宜。

translations.literal: Though Ji'an and the others are ill, slowly plan what is suitable.
translations.idiomatic: As for Ji'an and the others, though they are ill, deal with them gradually as circumstances allow.

sentences.zh: 定四方有天時，不可速也。」

translations.literal: Stabilizing the four directions has its heavenly timing—it cannot be rushed.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying the realm has its proper season; this cannot be forced.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，欲析鎮分建節度，使承宗歲輸賦如李師道。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and wished to divide Zhenzhou and establish separate military governorships, making Chengzong pay yearly tribute like Li Shidao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and planned to carve up Zhenzhou into separate commands, requiring Chengzong to pay annual tribute like Li Shidao.

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「假令承宗奉詔，諸道以割地同怨，是官爵虛出而無當也。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "Even if Chengzong obeyed the edict, the various circuits would resent the land being carved away—it would be giving offices and titles in vain with no gain.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang replied, "Even if Chengzong accepted, the other circuits would resent any partition of his territory—you would be handing out honors for nothing.

sentences.zh: 不如令使者諭之，無出上意。」

translations.literal: Better to have an envoy explain to him without revealing the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Better send an envoy to sound him out without revealing the throne's full design.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔京兆尹裴武慰撫，承宗奉詔恭甚，請上德、棣二州，遂以檢校工部尚書嗣領節度，而以德州刺史薛昌朝為保信軍節度使，統德、棣。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued an edict the Metropolitan Governor Pei Wu to comfort and reassure him; Chengzong received the edict with great deference, offered up the two prefectures of De and Di, and was thereupon made Acting Minister of Works to succeed to the military governorship, while Dezhou Prefect Xue Changchao was made military governor of the Baoxin Army, controlling De and Di.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Metropolitan Governor Pei Wu to reassure him. Chengzong received the edict with elaborate deference and offered De and Di prefectures. He was confirmed as Acting Minister of Works and military governor, while Dezhou Prefect Xue Changchao was made governor of the Baoxin Army over De and Di.

sentences.zh: 昌朝，嵩子也，與承宗故姻家，帝因欲離其親將，故命之。

translations.literal: Changchao was the son of Xue Song; he and Chengzong were old marriage kin—the emperor therefore wished to separate Chengzong from his close generals and so appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao was the son of Xue Song and an old in-law of Chengzong's family. The emperor meant to pry Chengzong from his trusted commanders and so sent him.

sentences.zh: 詔未至，承宗馳騎劫而歸，囚之。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived, Chengzong galloped with horsemen, intercepted him, and brought him back, imprisoning him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict could arrive, Chengzong sent riders to intercept Changchao, drag him back, and clap him in prison.

sentences.zh: 詔更用棣州刺史田渙為二州團練守捉使，遣中人傳詔令歸昌朝，承宗拒命，帝怒，詔削官爵，遣中人吐突承璀將左右神策，率河中、河陽、浙西、宣歙兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict then replaced him with Di Prefect Tian Huan as regimental commander and defense commissioner of the two prefectures, sent a eunuch to convey the edict ordering Changchao's release; Chengzong defied orders; the emperor was enraged, issued an edict stripping of offices and ranks, and sent the eunuch Tu Tu Chenghui to lead the Left and Right Shence Armies, together with troops from Hezhong, Heyang, Zhexi, and Xuanshe, to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The court then named Di Prefect Tian Huan regimental commander over the two prefectures and sent a eunuch with orders to free Changchao. Chengzong refused. The emperor stripped his titles and dispatched the eunuch Tu Tu Chenghui at the head of the Shence Armies, joined by forces from Hezhong, Heyang, Zhexi, and Xuanshe, to bring him to heel.

sentences.zh: 趙萬敵者，故武俊將，以健鬥聞，士真時入朝，上言討之必捷，令與承璀偕。

translations.literal: Zhao Wandu was a former general of Wujun's, famed for fierce fighting; when Shizhen was at court he memorialized that the attack would surely succeed, and Zhao was ordered to go with Chenghui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wandu, once a general under Wujun and renowned as a fierce fighter, was sent to join Chenghui after Shizhen, then at court, assured the emperor of a swift victory.

sentences.zh: 有詔：「武俊忠節茂著，其以實封賜子士則，毋毀墳墓。」

translations.literal: There was an edict: "Wujun's loyal merit is abundantly clear; let his fief of substance be granted to his son Shize, and do not destroy his tomb."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "Wujun's loyalty and merit are abundantly clear. Grant his substantive fief to his son Shize, and let his tomb be left untouched."

sentences.zh: 承璀至軍，無威略，師不振。

translations.literal: When Chenghui reached the army he had no martial strategy and the troops were not spirited.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghui reached the front without martial skill, and the army's spirit never rallied.

sentences.zh: 神策大將酈定進號驍將，以禽劉辟功，王陽山郡，至是戰北，馳而僨，趙人曰：「酈王也」，害之，師氣益折。

translations.literal: The Shence general Li Dingjin was styled a fierce commander; for capturing Liu Pi he was made Prince of Yangshan; this time he was defeated in the north, galloped and fell; the Zhao men said "It is the Prince of Li," and killed him; the army's morale was further broken.
translations.idiomatic: The Shence general Li Dingjin, famed as a fierce fighter and enfeoffed as Prince of Yangshan for capturing Liu Pi, was routed in the fighting, thrown from his horse in flight, and killed by Zhao troops who cried, "It is Prince Li!" The army's morale collapsed further.

sentences.zh: 及吳少誠死，李絳奏：「蔡無四鄰援，攻討勢易，不如赦承宗，專事淮西。」

translations.literal: When Wu Shaocheng died, Li Jiang memorialized: "Cai has no support from the four neighboring circuits; attack would be easy—better to pardon Chengzong and concentrate on Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Shaocheng's death Li Jiang urged, "Cai has no neighbors to aid it and would be easy to crush. Pardon Chengzong and focus the campaign on Huai West.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使盧從史市承宗，外自固，內實與之。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi Military Governor Lu Congshi traded with Chengzong—outwardly strengthening himself, inwardly in fact allied with him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi of Zhaoyi was dealing secretly with Chengzong—posing as the court's ally while actually in league with him.

sentences.zh: 太常卿權德輿諫曰：「神策兵市井屠販，不更戰陣，恐因勞憚遠，潰為盜賊。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Quan Deyu remonstrated, saying: "The Shence troops are market butchers and peddlers, untried in battle; I fear that wearied and dreading the distance they will collapse and become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Quan Deyu warned, "The Shence soldiers are townsmen and tradesmen with no battle experience. Wearied by a long campaign they may break and turn to banditry.

sentences.zh: 恒冀騎壯兵多，攻之必引時月，西戎乘間，則禁衛不可頓虛。

translations.literal: Heng and Ji have strong cavalry and many troops; attacking will surely take months; if the western barbarians seize the opportunity, the palace guard cannot be suddenly emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Heng-Ji fields powerful cavalry in great numbers; the siege will drag on for months. If western tribes strike while the capital guard is away, the throne will be left defenseless.

sentences.zh: 山東，疥癬也；

translations.literal: Shandong is a scab;
translations.idiomatic: The east is a skin rash—

sentences.zh: 京師，心腹也。

translations.literal: the capital is the heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: the capital is the heart itself.

sentences.zh: 不可不深念。

translations.literal: This cannot but be deeply considered.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must weigh this with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 且師出半年，費緡錢五百萬。

translations.literal: Moreover the army has been out half a year at a cost of five million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign has already run six months and consumed five million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 方夏甚暑水潦，疾疫且降，誠慮有潰橈之變。」

translations.literal: It is now high summer with great heat and floods; pestilence is about to descend—I truly fear there may be a collapse and mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: High summer brings brutal heat and flooding; plague will follow. I truly fear mutiny and rout.

sentences.zh: 又言：「山東諸侯，皆以息自副，人心不遠，誰肯為陛下盡力者。

translations.literal: He also said: "The lords east of the mountains all take Xi as their own deputy commissioners; men's hearts are not far from their own interests—who will exert himself fully for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Every eastern warlord keeps a trusted deputy close at hand—and their loyalty stays near home. Who will fight with all his might for the throne?

sentences.zh: 又盧從史倚寇為援，訹承璀邀寵利，宜召行營善將，令倍驛馳，度至半道，授以澤潞，而徙從史它鎮，破其奸圖，然後赦承宗，眾情必服。」

translations.literal: Moreover Lu Congshi relies on the rebel as support and coerces Chenghui for favor and profit; good generals from the expedition camp should be summoned, made to ride double relay at speed, and when halfway there be appointed to Zelu, while Congshi is transferred to another circuit to break his treacherous design; then pardon Chengzong and public sentiment will surely submit."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi is propping himself up on the rebel and bullying Chenghui for court favor. Summon able generals from the front, rush them by double relay, and halfway en route appoint them to Zelu while transferring Congshi elsewhere—break his intrigue, then pardon Chengzong, and the armies will fall in line."

sentences.zh: 帝未許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not yet agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not consent.

sentences.zh: 五年，河東軍拔其一屯，張茂昭破之木刀溝；

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Hedong army captured one of his outposts, and Zhang Maozhao defeated him at Mudao Gully;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Hedong army took one of Chengzong's outposts, and Zhang Maozhao routed him at Mudao Gully;

sentences.zh: 帝患從史詐，卒以計縛送京師；

translations.literal: the emperor, troubled by Congshi's deceit, finally by stratagem bound and sent him to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: troubled by Congshi's treachery, the emperor at last lured him into a trap, bound him, and sent him to the capital;

sentences.zh: 劉濟又拔安平。

translations.literal: Liu Ji also captured Anping.
translations.idiomatic: and Liu Ji captured Anping.

sentences.zh: 承宗懼，遣其屬崔遂上書謝罪，且言：「往年納地，迫三軍不得專，而為盧從史賣以求利，願請吏入賦得自新。」

translations.literal: Chengzong feared and sent his follower Cui Sui to submit a letter apologizing, saying moreover: "In past years when I yielded territory, the three armies forced me and I could not decide alone, while Lu Congshi sold it for profit; I wish to request officials and pay tribute so that I may renew myself.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Chengzong sent his aide Cui Sui with a letter of apology, claiming, "When I surrendered territory before, my three armies would not let me decide alone—and Lu Congshi sold the deal for his own gain. I beg to accept imperial officials and pay tribute so that I may start anew.

sentences.zh: 是時宿師久無功，餉不屬，帝憂之。

translations.literal: At this time the long-encamped army had achieved nothing for a long time and supplies did not continue; the emperor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: By then the expedition had stalled for months and supplies had run dry; the emperor grew anxious.

sentences.zh: 而淄青、盧龍數表請赦，乃詔浣雪，盡以故地畀之，罷諸道兵。

translations.literal: Ziqing and Lulong repeatedly submitted memorials requesting pardon; an edict then cleared the guilt, returned all the former territory, and dismissed the troops of the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqing and Lulong petitioned repeatedly for clemency. The emperor issued a pardon, restored all former lands, and recalled the allied armies.

sentences.zh: 昌朝歸京師，授右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Changchao returned to the capital and was appointed General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao was released to the capital and made a general of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 承宗見兵薄境，已而罷，歸罪從史，得不詰，自謂計得，謷然無顧憚。

translations.literal: Chengzong saw troops press the border, then they were dismissed; he blamed Congshi, escaped inquiry, considered his plan successful, and was arrogantly without scruple.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong had seen imperial troops mass on his border—then watched them withdraw. He pinned the blame on Congshi, escaped punishment, decided his gambit had worked, and swaggered without restraint.

sentences.zh: 七年，軍庫火，器鎧殆盡，殺守吏百餘人，不自安。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the army storehouse caught fire and weapons and armor were nearly all destroyed; more than a hundred guarding officials were killed; he was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the arsenal burned and nearly all arms and armor were lost; more than a hundred storekeepers were executed. Chengzong lived in uneasy dread.

sentences.zh: 及吳元濟反，承宗與李師道上書請宥，教其將尹少卿為蔡遊說，見宰相語不遜，武元衡怒，叱遣之。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji rebelled, Chengzong and Li Shidao submitted memorials requesting pardon for him; Chengzong instructed his general Yin Shaoqing to lobby on Cai's behalf; seeing the chancellor he spoke insolently; Wu Yuanheng was enraged and shouted him away.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji rose in rebellion, Chengzong and Li Shidao petitioned for his pardon. Chengzong sent his general Yin Shaoqing to plead Cai's case at court; Yin was insolent before the chancellor, and Wu Yuanheng furiously had him thrown out.

sentences.zh: 承宗怨甚，與師道謀，遣惡少年數十曹伏河陰，乘昏射吏，吏奔潰，因火漕院，人趣火所，鬥死者十餘輩，縣大發民捕盜，亡去不獲，凡敗錢三十萬緡、粟數萬斛。

translations.literal: Chengzong resented this deeply; with Shidao he plotted, sent several bands of vicious youths to lie in ambush at Heyin, and at dusk shot officials; the officials fled in rout; they then fired the grain depot; people rushed to the blaze; more than ten died fighting; the county greatly mobilized the people to catch the bandits but they escaped and were not taken; in all three hundred thousand strings of cash and several ten thousand bushels of grain were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Burning with resentment, Chengzong and Shidao sent gangs of ruffians to ambush Heyin. At dusk they shot at officials and set the grain depot ablaze. A dozen men died in the melee; the county raised a great hunt for the raiders but caught none. The damage ran to three hundred thousand strings of cash and tens of thousands of bushels of grain.

sentences.zh: 未幾，張晏等賊宰相元衡，京師大索，天子為旰食。

translations.literal: Before long Zhang Yan and others assassinated Chancellor Wu Yuanheng; the capital was searched on a grand scale; the Son of Heaven skipped meals in worry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhang Yan and his accomplices murdered Chancellor Wu Yuanheng. The capital was turned upside down in the search, and the emperor lost his appetite for days.

sentences.zh: 承宗嘗疏元衡過咎，留中。

translations.literal: Chengzong had once memorialized listing Wu Yuanheng's faults; it was kept within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong had earlier submitted a memorial denouncing Wu Yuanheng's failings; the emperor had kept it unread in the palace archives.

sentences.zh: 至是帝出表示群臣大議，鹹請聲其罪伐之。

translations.literal: At this the emperor issued a proclamation for the ministers to debate on a grand scale; all requested that his crimes be proclaimed and that he be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor now published an edict summoning the court to debate Chengzong's fate; all called for a formal condemnation and military action.

sentences.zh: 詔乃絕承宗朝貢，竄其弟承系、承迪、承榮於遠方，以博野、樂壽故范陽地，命歸劉總。

translations.literal: An edict then cut off Chengzong's tribute missions, exiled his younger brothers Chengxu, Chengdi, and Chengrong to distant places, and returned Boye, Leshou, and the former Fanyang lands to Liu Zong by command.
translations.idiomatic: The court severed Chengzong's tribute, banished his brothers Chengxu, Chengdi, and Chengrong to distant posts, and ordered Boye, Leshou, and the old Fanyang territories returned to Liu Zong.

sentences.zh: 而所遣盜處處竊發，斷建陵門戟，燔獻陵寢宮，伏甲欲反洛陽，不克。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the thieves he had sent erupted everywhere in secret raids, broke the halberds at the Jianling gate, burned the palace at the Xianling tomb, and hid armed men intending to seize Luoyang but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His agents struck everywhere—smashing the halberds at Jianling Gate, burning the lodge at Xianling, and planting armed men for a rising in Luoyang that failed.

sentences.zh: 承宗數出兵掠鄰鄙，田弘正上言承宗宜誅，帝使率師壓境。

translations.literal: Chengzong repeatedly sent troops to raid neighboring districts; Tian Hongzheng memorialized that Chengzong should be executed; the emperor ordered him to lead troops to press the border.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong raided his neighbors again and again. Tian Hongzheng urged that he be put to death, and the emperor ordered him to march and mass on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 承宗揣詔旨兵不即進，即肆剽滄、景、易、定間，人苦之。

translations.literal: Chengzong guessed from the edict's intent that the troops would not advance immediately, and at once wantonly plundered between Cang, Jing, Yi, and Ding; the people suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the edict as a bluff, Chengzong guessed the armies would not move at once and unleashed raids across Cang, Jing, Yi, and Ding. The people endured terrible suffering.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔削爵，以實封賜土平，使奉武俊後。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict stripped his noble rank, granted the substantive fief to Tuping, and made him continue Wujun's sacrificial line.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the court stripped Chengzong of his peerage, granted his fief to Tuping, and charged him with maintaining Wujun's ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 令河東、義武、盧龍、橫海、魏博、昭義六節度兵進討，大抵數十萬，環地數千里，以分其勢。

translations.literal: The six military governors of Hedong, Yiwu, Lulong, Henghai, Weibo, and Zhaoyi were ordered to advance in attack—altogether several hundred thousand men, encircling territory several thousand li across, to divide his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Six frontier commands—Hedong, Yiwu, Lulong, Henghai, Weibo, and Zhaoyi—were ordered to attack with several hundred thousand men, ringing his territory for thousands of li to divide his strength.

sentences.zh: 然營屯離置，主約不得一，故士觀望，獨昭義郗士美薄賊境，賊不敢犯。

translations.literal: Yet the camps were scattered and distant, the commanders' agreements were not unified, so the soldiers looked on without acting; only Zhaoyi's Xi Shimei pressed the rebel border, and the rebels did not dare violate it.
translations.idiomatic: But the camps lay scattered and their commanders could not agree; the troops hung back and watched. Only Xi Shimei of Zhaoyi pressed the rebel border hard enough that the enemy dared not cross it.

sentences.zh: 始，承宗不能葉諸父，皆奔京師。

translations.literal: At the beginning Chengzong could not detain his paternal uncles; they all fled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Chengzong could not keep hold of his paternal uncles; they all escaped to the capital.

sentences.zh: 士則為神策大將軍，聞其叛，請占數京兆，裴度請用為邢州刺史，使隸昭義，以傾趙人。

translations.literal: Shize was a great general of the Shence Army; hearing of the rebellion he requested to take up a post in Jingzhao; Pei Du recommended appointing him Prefect of Xingzhou, subordinate to Zhaoyi, to undermine the Zhao men.
translations.idiomatic: Shize, a Shence general, heard of the revolt and asked for a post in the capital region. Pei Du recommended him as prefect of Xingzhou under Zhaoyi to turn Zhao loyalties against Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 有王怡者，武俊從子，為承宗守南宮，士則招之，約歸命，謀泄遇害；

translations.literal: There was a Wang Yi, Wujun's nephew by a younger brother, who guarded Nangong for Chengzong; Shize recruited him and pledged submission; the plot leaked and he was killed;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, Wujun's nephew, held Nangong for Chengzong. Shize won him over with a promise of amnesty, but the plot was discovered and Yi was killed;

sentences.zh: 子元伯奔還，擢監察御史，詔贈怡尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: his son Yuanbo fled back and was promoted to Investigating Censor; an edict posthumously made Yi Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Yuanbo escaped to the court and was promoted to investigating censor; the throne posthumously honored Yi as Left Vice Minister of State.

sentences.zh: 明年元濟平，承宗大恐，使牙將石泛奉二子至魏博，因田弘正求入侍，且請歸德、棣二州，入租賦，待天子署吏。

translations.literal: The next year Yuanji was pacified; Chengzong was greatly afraid; he sent his gate general Shi Fan to escort his two sons to Weibo; through Tian Hongzheng he requested to attend court, and moreover asked to return the two prefectures of De and Di, pay rent and tribute, and await the Son of Heaven's appointment of officials.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, with Yuanji crushed, Chengzong was terrified. He sent his gate officer Shi Fan with his two sons to Weibo and, through Tian Hongzheng, begged to come to court, surrender De and Di, pay taxes, and accept imperial appointments.

sentences.zh: 弘正遣知感、知信詣闕下請命。

translations.literal: Hongzheng sent Zhigan and Zhixin to the palace to request orders.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng sent Zhigan and Zhixin to the capital to seek the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 前此，帝使尚書右丞崔從賜詔書許自新，承宗素服待罪。

translations.literal: Before this the emperor had sent Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Cui Cong to bestow an edict permitting renewal; Chengzong wore plain robes awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had sent Vice Director Cui Cong with an edict offering clemency; Chengzong had waited in plain robes to accept judgment.

sentences.zh: 及是乃詔復官爵，以華州刺史鄭權為橫海節度使，統德、棣、滄、景等州，復承宗實封戶三百，以所部饑，賜帛萬匹。

translations.literal: At this an edict restored offices and ranks; Huazhou Prefect Zheng Quan was made military governor of Henghai, controlling De, Di, Cang, Jing, and other prefectures; Chengzong's three hundred fief households of substance were restored; because his territory suffered famine, ten thousand bolts of silk were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court restored Chengzong's titles, made Huazhou Prefect Zheng Quan military governor of Henghai over De, Di, Cang, Jing, and neighboring prefectures, reinstated his three hundred fief households, and granted ten thousand bolts of silk because his people were starving.

sentences.zh: 李師道平，奉法益謹，表所領州錄事、參軍、判司、縣主簿、令，皆丐王官。

translations.literal: When Li Shidao was pacified, Chengzong observed the law all the more carefully; he memorialized listing the recorders, aides, judicial officers, county clerks, and magistrates of the prefectures he controlled, all requesting imperial appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shidao's fall Chengzong grew more scrupulous still. He submitted a roster of every recorder, aide, judicial officer, clerk, and magistrate in his domain, asking that the throne appoint them all.

sentences.zh: 十五年死，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of Yuanhe and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 軍中推其弟承元為留後。

translations.literal: The army pushed his younger brother Chengyuan as acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: The troops installed his younger brother Chengyuan as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 承元不敢世於鎮，詔用為義成軍節度使，事見本傳。

translations.literal: Chengyuan dared not hold the circuit in hereditary succession; an edict appointed him military governor of the Yicheng Army—the matter is recorded in his main biography.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan refused to inherit the command as family property; the court made him military governor of Yicheng—the full account appears in his main biography.

sentences.zh: 王廷湊，本回紇阿布思之族，隸安東都護府。

translations.literal: Wang Tingcou was originally of the Uyghur clan of Abu Si, subordinate to the Andong Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingcou came from the Uyghur clan of Abu Si and originally served under the Andong Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 曾祖五哥之，為李寶臣帳下，驍果善鬥，王武俊養為子，故冒姓王，世為裨將。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Wugezhi was under Li Baochen's command, brave and fierce and skilled in fighting; Wang Wujun raised him as a son, so he took the surname Wang; for generations they were vice-generals.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wugezhi had served in Li Baochen's camp as a fierce fighter; Wang Wujun adopted him as a son, and the family took the Wang surname and served for generations as staff officers.

sentences.zh: 廷湊生駢脅，沈鷙少言，喜讀《鬼谷》、兵家諸書。

translations.literal: Tingcou was born with fused ribs, deep and fierce and sparing of words; he delighted in reading the Guiguzi and various military books.
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou was born with conjoined ribs, grim and taciturn, and loved to study the Guiguzi and the military classics.

sentences.zh: 王承宗時，為兵馬使。

translations.literal: During Wang Chengzong's time he was horse-and-arms commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Chengzong he served as commissioner of cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 田弘正至鎮州，詔以度支緡錢百萬勞軍，不時致，廷湊暴其稽以觀眾心，眾果怨，由是害弘正，自稱留後，脅監軍表請節。

translations.literal: Tian Hongzheng arrived at Zhen Prefecture. An edict ordered one million strings of cash from the Treasury to reward the army, but it was not delivered on time. Tingcou exposed this delay to observe the troops' hearts; the masses indeed grew resentful. Thereby he killed Hongzheng, styled himself acting governor, and coerced the army supervisor into submitting a memorial requesting the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hongzheng reached Zhenzhou, the court had ordered a million strings of Treasury cash to reward the troops, but the payment did not arrive on schedule. Tingcou publicized the delay to test the army's mood; the men grew angry as he had hoped. He then murdered Hongzheng, declared himself acting military governor, and forced the army supervisor to memorialize the throne for a full commission.

sentences.zh: 又取冀州，殺刺史王進岌。

translations.literal: He also took Ji Prefecture and killed the prefect Wang Jingji.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized Ji Province and killed its prefect, Wang Jingji.

sentences.zh: 穆宗怒，以弘正子布為魏博節度使，率軍進討，仍敕橫海、昭義、河東、義武軍並力。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong was angry. He made Hongzheng's son Bu military governor of Weibo, led an army forward to attack and suppress them, and still ordered the Henghai, Zhaoyi, Hedong, and Yiwu armies to combine their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong was furious. He appointed Hongzheng's son Tian Bu military governor of Weibo and sent him to lead a punitive campaign, while ordering the Henghai, Zhaoyi, Hedong, and Yiwu commands to join the effort.

sentences.zh: 於是大將王位等謀執廷湊，不克，死者三千餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the senior general Wang Wei and others plotted to seize Tingcou. They did not succeed; more than three thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Senior generals including Wang Wei then plotted to seize Tingcou, but the attempt failed and more than three thousand men were killed.

sentences.zh: 會朱克融囚張弘靖，以幽州亂，乃合從拒王師。

translations.literal: Just then Zhu Kerong imprisoned Zhang Hongjing, and with You Prefecture in disorder, they then allied together to resist the imperial armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Zhu Kerong imprisoned Zhang Hongjing and threw Youzhou into chaos; the rebels then joined forces to resist the imperial armies.

sentences.zh: 有詔議攻討先後，劍南東川節度使王涯以為「范陽亂非宿謀，可先事鎮州，又有魏博之怨，濟以晉陽、滄德，掎角而進。

translations.literal: There was an edict to debate the order of attack and suppression. Wang Ya, military governor of Jiannan East Circuit, held that "the Fanyang disorder was not a long-laid plan; one may first deal with Zhen Prefecture. There is also Weibo's resentment to draw on, aided by Jinyang and Cangde, advancing in pincer fashion.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a debate on campaign priorities. Wang Ya, military governor of eastern Jiannan, argued: "The uprising in Fanyang was not long premeditated. We should strike Zhenzhou first. We can also exploit Weibo's grievance, with Jinyang and Cangde as supports, and advance in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 夫用兵若鬥然，先扼喉領。

translations.literal: In employing troops it is like a fight—one first seizes the throat and neck.
translations.idiomatic: In war, as in a brawl, one must first seize the enemy by the throat.

sentences.zh: 今瀛莫、易定實賊咽喉，宜屯重兵，俾死生不得相聞，間諜不入，此莫勝之策。」

translations.literal: Now Yingmo and Yiding are truly the rebels' throat; heavy troops should be stationed so that life and death cannot be heard between them and spies cannot enter. This is the most unbeatable strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Yingmo and Yiding are the rebels' jugular. Station heavy forces there so their lines cannot communicate and no spy can pass through—that is the surest strategy.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔義武節度使陳楚閉境，督諸軍三道攻。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Chen Chu, military governor of Yiwu, to close the borders and supervise the armies attacking in three columns.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this counsel and ordered Chen Chu, military governor of Yiwu, to seal the borders and direct a three-pronged assault.

sentences.zh: 而滄德烏重胤最宿將，當一面。

translations.literal: Wu Chongyin of Cangde was the most seasoned veteran and was assigned one front.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin of Cangde, the most experienced commander among them, was given one front.

sentences.zh: 裴度以河東節度使兼幽、鎮招撫使，屯承天軍。

translations.literal: Pei Du, as Hedong military governor and concurrently commissioner for pacification of You and Zhen, encamped at Chengtian Army.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du served as Hedong military governor and concurrently as commissioner for pacifying You and Zhen, encamping at Chengtian Army.

sentences.zh: 重胤知時不可，案兵未肯前，帝浮於聽受，銳克伐，更以深冀行營節度使杜叔良代之。

translations.literal: Chongyin knew the time was not right, held his troops and would not advance. The emperor was shallow in what he heard and accepted, eager for quick victory, and replaced him with Du Shuliang, field-command military governor of Shen and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin knew conditions were unfavorable and kept his army in camp, refusing to advance. The emperor, too easily swayed by what he heard, was impatient for victory and replaced him with Du Shuliang, field commander of Shen and Ji.

sentences.zh: 叔良素結中人，入見帝，大言曰：「賊不足破！」

translations.literal: Shuliang had long cultivated ties with palace insiders. Entering to see the emperor, he spoke boldly: "The rebels are not worth breaking!
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang had long cultivated palace eunuchs. When he was received by the emperor he declared boldly, "These rebels are hardly worth defeating!

sentences.zh: 會度逐廷湊兵於會星，又入元氏，焚壁二十二。

translations.literal: Just then Pei Du drove Tingcou's troops at Huixing, then entered Yuanshi and burned twenty-two fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Pei Du routed Tingcou's forces at Huixing, entered Yuanshi, and burned twenty-two fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 叔良率諸道兵救深州，戰博野，大奔，失所持節，以身免，貶歸州刺史。

translations.literal: Shuliang led troops from the various circuits to relieve Shen Prefecture. At the battle of Boye there was a great rout; he lost the commission baton he held, escaped with his body, and was demoted to prefect of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang led allied troops to relieve Shenzhou, but at Boye his army was routed. He lost his commission baton and barely escaped with his life, then was demoted to prefect of Gui.

sentences.zh: 叔良者，將家子，本以附會至靈武節度使，坐不職罷，復階貴近，帥滄景。

translations.literal: Shuliang was the son of a general's family. Originally through currying favor he reached military governor of Lingwu; dismissed for failure in office, he again climbed through the powerful and near, and commanded Cang and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang came from a military family. He had first risen to military governor of Lingwu through flattery and connections, was dismissed for incompetence, then climbed again through court favor and was put in command of Cang and Jing.

sentences.zh: 廷湊知其怯，故先犯之，師由是敗。

translations.literal: Tingcou knew his cowardice, and for that reason first struck at him; the armies were thereby defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou knew Shuliang was a coward and struck at him first; the imperial campaign collapsed as a result.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝賜賚無藝，府帑空，既集諸道兵，調發火馳，民不堪其勞。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's gifts and rewards knew no limit; the treasury was empty. Once troops from the various circuits had been gathered, mobilization orders flew like fire, and the people could not bear the labor.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor's rewards had become boundless and the treasury was empty. With troops mustered from every circuit, mobilization orders flew out like wildfire, and the people could no longer endure the burden.

sentences.zh: 仰度支者大抵兵十五萬，有司懼不給，置南北供軍院。

translations.literal: Those dependent on the Treasury amounted to roughly a hundred and fifty thousand troops. The bureaus feared supplies would not suffice and established Northern and Southern Commissary Offices for the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly a hundred and fifty thousand soldiers depended on the Treasury for support. Fearing the funds would not suffice, the bureaus established separate northern and southern army supply offices.

sentences.zh: 既薄賊鄙，餉道梗棘，樵蘇不繼，兵番休取芻蒸。

translations.literal: Once they drew near the rebels' borders, supply routes were obstructed and thorn-choked; fuel and fodder could not continue, and troops on rest rotations were sent to gather hay and kindling.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies neared rebel territory, supply lines became choked and impassable. Fuel and fodder ran short, and soldiers on rest rotation were sent out to gather hay and firewood.

sentences.zh: 廷湊乘間奪轉運車六百乘，食愈困，至所須衣帛，未半道，諸軍強取之，有司弗能制。

translations.literal: Tingcou seized the opportunity to capture six hundred transport wagons. Food grew ever more distressed; even the required clothing and silks, before halfway on the road, the various armies forcibly took them, and the officials could not control it.
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou seized six hundred supply wagons when the chance arose. Hunger worsened; even clothing and silks intended for the troops were forcibly taken by the armies before they were halfway to camp, and the officials could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 其縣師深入者，不得衣食。

translations.literal: Among the imperial armies, those who penetrated deeply obtained neither food nor clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial units that pushed deep into enemy territory went without food or clothing.

sentences.zh: 又監軍宦人，悉取精票士自隨，疲瑣者備行陣，戰輒潰。

translations.literal: Moreover the supervising eunuchs all took the choicest strong soldiers for themselves, while the weak and petty filled the battle lines; in battle they immediately broke.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising eunuchs kept the best soldiers for their personal retinues and left the weak and worthless to fill the ranks; in battle those lines collapsed at once.

sentences.zh: 二賊眾不過萬餘，王師統制不一，訖無功。

translations.literal: The two rebels' forces numbered no more than ten thousand-odd, yet the imperial armies lacked unified command and in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The two rebel bands numbered barely ten thousand men, yet the imperial armies lacked unified command and achieved nothing in the end.

sentences.zh: 宰相不知兵，為異議搖訹，裁報乖戾，深州圍益急。

translations.literal: The chief ministers did not understand warfare; they raised differing opinions that shook and confused, and imperial decisions and replies were perverse; the siege of Shen Prefecture grew ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers knew nothing of war. Their conflicting advice sowed confusion, court orders grew erratic, and the siege of Shenzhou tightened by the day.

sentences.zh: 明年，魏牙將史憲誠叛，田布眾潰於南宮。

translations.literal: The next year the Wei tooth-general Shi Xiancheng rebelled, and Tian Bu's forces disintegrated at Nangong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shi Xiancheng, a Wei staff general, rebelled, and Tian Bu's army disintegrated at Nangong.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，乃赦廷湊，檢校右散騎常侍、成德軍節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice; he then pardoned Tingcou and appointed him acting Right Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and military governor of the Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice but to pardon Tingcou and appoint him acting Right Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and military governor of the Chengde Army.

sentences.zh: 會牛元翼出奔，廷湊遂取深州，詔兵部侍郎韓愈慰其軍。

translations.literal: When Niu Yuanji fled in escape, Tingcou then took Shen Prefecture. An edict ordered Han Yu, Vice Minister of War, to comfort the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Niu Yuanji fled, Tingcou seized Shenzhou. The court ordered Han Yu, Vice Minister of War, to go and reassure the army.

sentences.zh: 廷湊既原，則稍挺，與克融、憲誠深相結，為輔車援。

translations.literal: Once Tingcou had been pardoned, he then grew somewhat bolder, formed deep ties with Kerong and Xiancheng, and became mutual wheel-and-axle support.
translations.idiomatic: Once pardoned, Tingcou grew bolder still. He forged close ties with Kerong and Xiancheng and the three became mutual supports, like wheels locked together.

sentences.zh: 滄州李全略死，子同捷求襲，文宗不許，更授兗海節度使。

translations.literal: Li Quanlue of Cang Prefecture died. His son Tongjie sought to succeed him; Emperor Wenzong did not permit it and instead appointed him military governor of Yan and Hai.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Quanlue of Cangzhou died, his son Tongjie sought to succeed him. Emperor Wenzong refused and instead appointed him military governor of Yan and Hai.

sentences.zh: 同捷逆命，乃以珍幣子女厚結廷湊，帝虞其變，故授檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Tongjie defied the order. He then used precious gifts and women to bind Tingcou closely. The emperor feared a shift and therefore granted him the acting title of Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjie defied the order and lavished precious gifts and women on Tingcou to cement their alliance. Fearing a shift in loyalties, the emperor granted Tingcou the acting title of Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 及幽、魏、徐、兗兵討同捷，廷湊橈魏北鄙以牽制之，而饋滄景鹺糧，囚鄰道使者不遣。

translations.literal: When troops from You, Wei, Xu, and Yan marched to suppress Tongjie, Tingcou harassed Wei's northern border to pin them down, while supplying Cang and Jing with salt and grain, and detained envoys from neighboring circuits without releasing them.
translations.idiomatic: When armies from You, Wei, Xu, and Yan marched against Tongjie, Tingcou raided Wei's northern frontier to pin them down, supplied Cang and Jing with salt and grain, and detained envoys from neighboring circuits without releasing them.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詔絕其輸貢。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered an end to accepting his tribute deliveries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered that Tingcou's tribute be cut off.

sentences.zh: 於是易定、柳公濟戰新樂，斬首三千級。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Gongji of Yiding fought at Xinle and took three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongji of Yiding then fought at Xinle and took three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 昭義劉從諫戰臨城，敗之，引漳註深、冀。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi fought at Lincheng, defeated them, and diverted the Zhang River to flood Shen and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi fought at Lincheng, routed the enemy, and diverted the Zhang River to flood Shen and Ji.

sentences.zh: 有詔：「同捷亂，廷湊同惡，宜削官爵，諸道以兵進討，有能斬廷湊者，賜錢二萬緡，優畀之官；

translations.literal: There was an edict: "Tongjie has rebelled; Tingcou shares the evil. Both should be stripped of rank and title. The various circuits shall advance with troops to attack and suppress them. Whoever can behead Tingcou shall receive twenty thousand strings of cash and be preferentially granted office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Tongjie has rebelled and Tingcou is his accomplice. Strip them both of rank and title. Every circuit shall march against them. Whoever beheads Tingcou shall receive twenty thousand strings of cash and be preferentially granted office.

sentences.zh: 以州鎮降者，等差為比。」

translations.literal: Those who surrender prefectures or garrisons shall be rewarded on a graded scale by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Those who surrender prefectures or garrisons shall be rewarded on a graded scale.

sentences.zh: 公濟再戰行唐，皆克，焚柵十五。

translations.literal: Gongji fought again at Xingtang, winning each time, and burned fifteen palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Gongji fought again at Xingtang, won both engagements, and burned fifteen palisades.

sentences.zh: 廷湊射蠟書求救於幽州，行營李載義獲之；

translations.literal: Tingcou shot a wax-sealed letter seeking rescue to You Prefecture; Li Zaiyi of the field camp captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou sent a wax-sealed plea for aid to Youzhou by arrow; Li Zaiyi of the field camp intercepted it.

sentences.zh: 又納魏叛將丌志沼。

translations.literal: He also received Qi Zhizhao, the rebel general of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He also took in Qi Zhizhao, a rebel general from Wei.

sentences.zh: 會同捷平，廷湊稍畏，表上景州，而弓高、樂陵、長河三縣固守，復上書謝。

translations.literal: When Tongjie was pacified, Tingcou grew somewhat fearful, memorialized surrendering Jing Prefecture, but the three counties of Gonggao, Leling, and Changhe held firm; he submitted another letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongjie was suppressed, Tingcou grew fearful. He memorialized offering up Jing Prefecture, but the three counties of Gonggao, Leling, and Changhe held out; he submitted another letter of apology.

sentences.zh: 帝方厭兵，赦之，悉復官爵，還所上州。

translations.literal: The emperor was then weary of war, pardoned him, fully restored rank and title, and returned the prefecture he had offered up.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, weary of war, pardoned him, fully restored his rank and title, and returned the prefecture he had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 久之，進兼太子太傅、太原郡公。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 鎮冀自惟嶽以來，拒天子命，然重鄰好，畏法，稍屈則祈自新。

translations.literal: Since Wei Yue, Zhen and Ji had defied the Son of Heaven's orders, yet they valued neighborly ties, feared the law, and when slightly pressed would petition for renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei Yue's day, Zhen and Ji had defied imperial orders, yet they valued good relations with neighbors, feared the law, and when pressed would petition for renewal.

sentences.zh: 至廷湊湊資兇悖，肆毒甘亂，不臣不仁，雖夷狄不若也。

translations.literal: When it came to Tingcou—by nature fierce and rebellious, who spread poison and delighted in disorder, neither loyal subject nor humane man—even the barbarian tribes were not his equal.
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou was another matter: by nature cruel and defiant, he delighted in spreading poison and chaos. Neither loyal subject nor humane ruler—even the barbarians were not his equal in wickedness.

sentences.zh: 大和八年死，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dahe he died; posthumously appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of the Dahe era and was posthumously appointed Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 軍中以元逵請命，帝聽襲節度。

translations.literal: The army petitioned with Yuan Kui's name; the emperor approved his succession to the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: The army petitioned on behalf of Yuan Kui, and the emperor approved his succession to the command.

sentences.zh: 元逵，其次子也。

translations.literal: Yuan Kui was his second son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Kui was his second son.

sentences.zh: 識禮法，歲時貢獻如職。

translations.literal: He understood rites and law, and rendered seasonal tribute and offerings as duty required.
translations.idiomatic: He understood ritual and law and rendered seasonal tribute as duty required.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，詔尚絳王悟女壽安公主。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and ordered him wed to Princess Shou'an, daughter of Prince Jiang of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and ordered him married to Princess Shou'an, daughter of Prince Jiang of Wu.

sentences.zh: 元逵遣人納聘闕下，進千盤食、良馬、主妝澤奩具、奴婢，議者嘉其恭。

translations.literal: Yuan Kui sent men to the capital to deliver betrothal gifts, presenting a thousand platters of food, fine horses, the princess's dowry chest and its ornaments, and servants and maids. Commentators praised his deference.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Kui sent envoys to the capital with betrothal gifts—a thousand platters of food, fine horses, the princess's dowry chest and ornaments, and servants and maids. Observers praised his deference.

sentences.zh: 其後劉稹叛，武宗詔元逵為北面招討使。

translations.literal: Later, when Liu Zhen rebelled, Emperor Wuzong appointed Yuan Kui northern campaign commissioner for suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Liu Zhen rebelled, Emperor Wuzong appointed Yuan Kui northern campaign commissioner for suppression.

sentences.zh: 詔下，即日師引道，拔宣務壁，破援軍堯山，攻邢州降之，累遷檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, that very day he marched forth, captured the fortifications at Xuanwu, routed the relief army at Yaoshan, attacked Xing Prefecture until it submitted, and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Minister of Education and Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The moment the edict was issued he marched forth, captured the fort at Xuanwu, routed the relief force at Yaoshan, and attacked Xingzhou until it submitted. He was repeatedly promoted, eventually to Acting Minister of Education and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 稹平，加兼太子太師，封太原郡公，食實封戶二百，進至兼太傅。

translations.literal: When Zhen was pacified, he was further made concurrent Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery with two hundred households of substantive fief, and advanced to concurrent Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhen was pacified, he was further made concurrent Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery with two hundred substantive fief households, and advanced to concurrent Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 大中八年死，年四十三，贈太師，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong he died at age forty-three; posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of the Dazhong era at age forty-three, was posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor, and was given the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子紹鼎襲，字嗣先，累擢檢校尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: His son Shaoding succeeded him, style name Sixian, and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaoding succeeded him. Style name Sixian, he was repeatedly promoted to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 其為人淫湎自放，性暴，厚裒斂，升樓彈射路人以為樂。

translations.literal: In character he was debauched and unrestrained, by nature violent; he taxed heavily and would climb a tower to shoot at passersby for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He was debauched and unrestrained by nature, violent in temper, and taxed heavily. For amusement he would climb a tower and shoot at passersby.

sentences.zh: 眾忿其虐，欲逐之。

translations.literal: The troops resented his cruelty and wished to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: The troops resented his cruelty and wanted to drive him out.

sentences.zh: 會病死，贈司空。

translations.literal: He happened to die of illness and was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness and was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子幼未能事，宣宗以元逵次子紹懿為留後以嗣，俄為節度使，累封太原縣伯，加檢校司空。

translations.literal: His son was young and could not manage affairs. Emperor Xuanzong appointed Yuan Kui's second son Shaoyi as acting governor to succeed him; soon he became military governor, was repeatedly enfeoffed as Count of Taiyuan County, and given the acting title Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son was too young to govern. Emperor Xuanzong appointed Yuan Kui's second son Shaoyi as acting governor to succeed him; he soon became military governor, was repeatedly enfeoffed as Count of Taiyuan County, and was given the acting title Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 政簡易，咸通七年死，贈司徒。

translations.literal: His government was simple and easygoing. In the seventh year of Xiantong he died; posthumously appointed Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was simple and easygoing. He died in the seventh year of the Xiantong era and was posthumously appointed Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 以紹鼎子景崇嗣。

translations.literal: Shaoding's son Jingchong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoding's son Jingchong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 初，紹懿病篤，召景崇曰：「先君以政屬我，須爾長，將授之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shaoyi was gravely ill, he summoned Jingchong and said: "Your forefather entrusted governance to me, intending when you came of age to hand it over to you.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyi was gravely ill, he summoned Jingchong and said, "Your forefather entrusted the command to me, intending to hand it over to you when you came of age.

sentences.zh: 今疾甚，爾雖少，勉總軍務，禮藩鄰，奉朝廷，則家業不墜矣。」

translations.literal: Now my illness is grave. Though you are still young, strive to oversee military affairs, treat neighboring prefectures with courtesy, and serve the court—then our family's enterprise will not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Now my illness is grave. Though you are still young, strive to oversee military affairs, treat neighboring prefectures with courtesy, and serve the court—then our family's enterprise will not fall.

sentences.zh: 監軍上狀，懿宗悅，擢景崇為留後，尋進節度使。

translations.literal: The army supervisor memorialized the facts. Emperor Yizong was pleased and promoted Jingchong to acting governor; soon after he was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor reported this to the throne. Emperor Yizong was pleased and promoted Jingchong to acting governor; soon after he was made military governor.

sentences.zh: 景崇，字孟安，以公主嫡孫，尤被寵。

translations.literal: Jingchong, style name Meng'an, was especially favored as the princess's eldest grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong, style name Meng'an, was especially favored at court as the princess's eldest grandson.

sentences.zh: 龐勛反，景崇遣兵會王師平賊，進檢校尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun rebelled, Jingchong sent troops to join the imperial armies in pacifying the rebels and was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun rebelled, Jingchong sent troops to join the imperial campaign against him and was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 主薨，謚曰章惠，景崇居喪如禮。

translations.literal: The princess died; posthumously titled Gracious and Kind. Jingchong observed mourning as rites prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess died, she was posthumously titled Gracious and Kind. Jingchong observed mourning as ritual prescribed.

sentences.zh: 母張卒，號慕羸惙，當時稱之。

translations.literal: When his mother Lady Zhang died, he wailed and mourned until he was wasted and gaunt; men of the time praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother Lady Zhang died, he wailed in grief until he was wasted and gaunt; men of the time praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 以政委賓佐，檢戒親屬不得與。

translations.literal: He entrusted governance to staff officers and strictly warned his kinsmen not to interfere.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted governance to his staff and strictly warned his kinsmen not to interfere.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲引母昆弟為牙將，其佐張位曰：「軍中用人，有勞有能，若私其人，厚畀田宅祿食可也，何必以官。」

translations.literal: Once he wished to appoint his mother's brothers as tooth generals. His aide Zhang Wei said: "In the army, men are chosen for merit and ability. If you favor someone personally, generous grants of fields, dwellings, stipends, and provisions will suffice—why must you give them office?
translations.idiomatic: Once he wished to appoint his mother's brothers as staff generals. His aide Zhang Wei said, "In the army, men are chosen for merit and ability. If you wish to favor someone personally, grant him fields, dwellings, stipends, and provisions—but why give him an office?

sentences.zh: 景崇謝。

translations.literal: Jingchong apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong apologized and withdrew the plan.

sentences.zh: 進同中書門下平章事、檢校太尉兼中書令，封趙國公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Associate Grand Councilor, Acting Grand Marshal and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Associate Grand Councilor, Acting Grand Marshal and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 乾符五年，進王常山。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianfu he was elevated to Prince of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Qianfu era he was elevated to Prince of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 黃巢反，帝西狩，偽使賫詔至，景崇斬以徇，因發兵馳檄諸道，合定州處存連師西入關，問行在，貢輸相踵。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao rebelled, the emperor fled west; a false envoy arrived bearing a forged edict. Jingchong executed him publicly as a warning, then mobilized troops and dispatched urgent proclamations to every circuit, joining Wang Chucun of Ding Prefecture to lead their armies west through the passes, inquiring after the emperor's whereabouts; tribute and supplies arrived in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao rebelled and the emperor fled west, a false envoy arrived bearing a forged edict. Jingchong executed him publicly as a warning, then mobilized his troops and sent urgent proclamations to every circuit. He joined Wang Chucun of Dingzhou to lead their armies west through the passes, inquiring after the emperor's whereabouts while tribute and supplies arrived in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 每語及宗廟園陵，輒流涕。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of the imperial ancestral temples and tombs, tears would come.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of the imperial ancestral temples and tombs, tears would come to his eyes.

sentences.zh: 蔚州刺史蘇祐為沙陀所攻，乞師於幽州，屯美女谷，兵不利。

translations.literal: Su You, prefect of Yu Prefecture, was attacked by the Shatuo and begged troops from You Prefecture; he encamped at Meinü Valley but his army fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: Su You, prefect of Yu Prefecture, was attacked by the Shatuo and begged troops from Youzhou. He encamped at Meinü Valley, but his army fared poorly.

sentences.zh: 祐將出奔，會詔徙濮州刺史，擁兵之官，道於鎮，景崇館於靈壽，肆其下剽奪，景崇殺之。

translations.literal: You was about to flee when suddenly an edict transferred him to prefect of Pu Prefecture. He marched to his new post at the head of his troops. Passing through the garrison, Jingchong hosted him at Lingshou—but You let his men plunder at will, and Jingchong had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: You was about to flee when an edict suddenly transferred him to prefect of Pu. He marched to his new post at the head of his troops. Passing through the garrison, Jingchong hosted him at Lingshou, but You let his men plunder freely; Jingchong had him killed.

sentences.zh: 嗣節度凡十四年，十三遷至檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In all, he held the military commission for fourteen years and rose through thirteen promotions to Acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He held the command for fourteen years in all and rose through thirteen promotions to Acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 中和三年死，年三十七，贈太傅，謚曰忠穆。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhonghe he died at age thirty-seven; posthumously appointed Grand Tutor, with the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Zhonghe era at age thirty-seven, was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor, and was given the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 子镕。

translations.literal: His son was Rong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Rong.

sentences.zh: 镕年十歲，軍中推為留後，授檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: Rong was ten years old; the army acclaimed him acting governor and he was appointed Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was ten years old when the army acclaimed him acting governor and he was appointed Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 李克用、楊復光攻黃巢，镕凡再饋粟以濟師。

translations.literal: When Li Keyong and Yang Fuguang attacked Huang Chao, Rong twice supplied grain to sustain their armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong and Yang Fuguang attacked Huang Chao, Rong twice supplied grain to sustain their armies.

sentences.zh: 僖宗還自蜀，獻馬牛戎械萬計。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu, Rong presented tens of thousands of horses, oxen, and weapons of war.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu, Rong presented tens of thousands of horses, oxen, and weapons of war.

sentences.zh: 於是克用方擊孟方立於邢州，镕歸芻糧。

translations.literal: At that time Keyong was attacking Meng Fangli at Xing Prefecture; Rong sent fodder and grain back to him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Keyong was attacking Meng Fangli at Xingzhou, and Rong sent him fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 邢州平，克用遂謀山東，屯常山西，引輕騎涉滹沱諜軍，會大澍，平地水出，镕兵奄至，克用匿林中以免。

translations.literal: When Xing Prefecture was pacified, Keyong then plotted in the Shandong region, encamped west of Mount Chang, and led light cavalry across the Hutuo to spy on the armies. A great downpour came; water rose across the flat ground. Rong's troops suddenly closed in; Keyong hid in a forest and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingzhou was pacified, Keyong turned his ambitions toward the east, encamped west of Mount Chang, and led light cavalry across the Hutuo to reconnoiter the armies. A great downpour flooded the plain. Rong's troops suddenly closed in, and Keyong hid in a forest to escape.

sentences.zh: 是時，幽州李匡威亦謀取易、定分其地。

translations.literal: At this time Li Kuangwei of You Prefecture also plotted to seize Yi and Ding and carve up their territory.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Kuangwei of Youzhou also plotted to seize Yi and Ding and carve up their territory.

sentences.zh: 王處存方厚事克用，克用寵將李存孝已拔邢，則略镕南鄙，別將李存信等出井陘會之。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun was then lavishing service on Keyong. Keyong's favored general Li Cunxiao, having already taken Xing, raided the southern border of Rong's domain while another commander Li Cunxin and others came out through Jingxing to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun was then lavishing favors on Keyong. Keyong's favored general Li Cunxiao, having already taken Xing, raided Rong's southern border while another commander, Li Cunxin, and others came out through Jingxing to join him.

sentences.zh: 镕侵堯山，存孝擊敗之，遂至深、越。

translations.literal: Rong attacked Yaoshan; Cunxiao defeated him and pushed on to Shen and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Rong attacked Yaoshan, but Cunxiao defeated him and pushed on into Shen and Yue.

sentences.zh: 镕求救於匡威。

translations.literal: Rong sought rescue from Kuangwei.
translations.idiomatic: Rong begged Kuangwei for rescue.

sentences.zh: 存孝方攻臨城等數縣，聞匡威屯鄗，引師去。

translations.literal: Cunxiao was attacking several counties including Lincheng when he heard Kuangwei was encamped at Hao; he withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao was attacking several counties including Lincheng when he heard Kuangwei was encamped at Hao; he withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 存信素忌存孝，妄曰「無擊賊意。」

translations.literal: Cunxin had long been jealous of Cunxiao and falsely claimed: "He has no intention of attacking the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin had long been jealous of Cunxiao and falsely claimed, "He has no intention of attacking the enemy.

sentences.zh: 克用信之。

translations.literal: Keyong believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong believed him.

sentences.zh: 存孝，飛狐人，所謂安敬思者，善騎射，攻葛從周，敗張浚、韓建，數有奇功。

translations.literal: Cunxiao, a native of Feihu—the man known as An Jingsi—excelled at mounted archery; he had attacked Ge Congzhou and defeated Zhang Jun and Han Jian, winning many extraordinary feats.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao, a native of Feihu—the man known as An Jingsi—excelled at mounted archery. He had attacked Ge Congzhou and defeated Zhang Jun and Han Jian, winning many extraordinary victories.

sentences.zh: 至是懼讒，挈邢州歸朱全忠，並結镕為助。

translations.literal: Now fearing slander, he took Xing Prefecture over to Zhu Quanzhong and also allied with Rong for support.
translations.idiomatic: Now fearing slander, he surrendered Xingzhou to Zhu Quanzhong and also allied with Rong for support.

sentences.zh: 天子詔出鎮、幽、魏兵援之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered troops from Zhen, You, and Wei to march out in relief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered troops from Zhen, You, and Wei to march out in relief.

sentences.zh: 景福元年，克用假道於镕，以討存孝，镕不答，乃與處存連兵侵镕，拔堅固鎮，攻新市。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingfu, Keyong requested passage through Rong's territory to attack Cunxiao; Rong did not reply. Keyong then joined Chucun to invade Rong's lands, captured Jian'gu Fort, and attacked Xinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jingfu era, Keyong requested passage through Rong's territory to attack Cunxiao; Rong did not reply. Keyong then joined Chucun to invade Rong's lands, captured Jian'gu Fort, and attacked Xinshi.

sentences.zh: 镕禽克用將薛萬金。

translations.literal: Rong captured Keyong's general Xue Wanjin.
translations.idiomatic: Rong captured Keyong's general Xue Wanjin.

sentences.zh: 匡威以兵三萬救镕。

translations.literal: Kuangwei came with thirty thousand troops to rescue Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei marched with thirty thousand troops to rescue Rong.

sentences.zh: 克用自攻常山，度滹沱。

translations.literal: Keyong personally attacked Changshan and crossed the Hutuo.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong personally attacked Changshan and crossed the Hutuo.

sentences.zh: 镕引騎十萬夜濟礠水，襲敗之，斬二萬級，奪鎧器三百乘，克用退壁欒城。

translations.literal: Rong led one hundred thousand horsemen, crossed the Ci River by night, and struck in surprise to defeat him; twenty thousand heads were taken, three hundred cartloads of armor and weapons were seized, and Keyong withdrew to fortify Luancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rong led one hundred thousand horsemen across the Ci River by night and routed Keyong's force, taking twenty thousand heads and three hundred cartloads of armor and weapons. Keyong pulled back and fortified Luancheng.

sentences.zh: 天子有詔和解三鎮，克用還，然未得誌，故復伐镕。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven issued an edict to reconcile the three garrisons; Keyong returned, yet had not achieved his aim, and therefore again attacked Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict ordering reconciliation among the three garrisons, and Keyong withdrew—but his ambition remained unfulfilled, so he attacked Rong again.

sentences.zh: 匡威以五千騎敗克用於元氏，镕具牛酒會匡威槁城，餉金二十萬以謝。

translations.literal: Kuangwei with five thousand horsemen defeated Keyong at Yuanshi. Rong prepared oxen and wine to meet Kuangwei at Gaocheng and sent two hundred thousand in gold as thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei defeated Keyong at Yuanshi with five thousand horsemen. Rong prepared a feast of oxen and wine to welcome him at Gaocheng and sent two hundred thousand strings of gold in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 俄而匡威為弟匡籌所逐，镕德其助己，迎而館之。

translations.literal: Before long Kuangwei was driven out by his younger brother Kuangchou. Rong was grateful for his help and welcomed him to lodge with him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kuangchou drove his brother Kuangwei from power. Grateful for the aid Kuangwei had given him, Rong welcomed him and lodged him in his own residence.

sentences.zh: 匡威親忌日，镕往吊，伏起，殺其府屬楊洽及親吏淡從，有甲者牽镕袖。

translations.literal: On the death anniversary of Kuangwei's parent, Rong went to offer condolences; men lying in ambush rose up and killed his staff member Yang Qia and close officer Dan Cong. An armored man seized Rong by the sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: On the anniversary of Kuangwei's parent's death, Rong came to offer condolences. Ambushers sprang up and killed his staff member Yang Qia and his close officer Dan Cong. An armored man grabbed Rong by the sleeve.

sentences.zh: 匡威曰：「與我四州，可不死！」

translations.literal: Kuangwei said: "Give me four prefectures and you need not die!"
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei said, "Cede four prefectures to me and you may live!"

sentences.zh: 镕許之。

translations.literal: Rong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong agreed.

sentences.zh: 將镕入牙城，鎮軍噪而闔左門，坎垣出戰。

translations.literal: As they were leading Rong into the yamen fortress, the garrison troops clamored, barred the left gate, breached the wall, and sallied out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: As they were leading Rong into the headquarters fortress, the garrison troops raised a clamor, barred the left gate, broke through the wall, and sallied out to fight.

sentences.zh: 會大雨風，木拔瓦飛。

translations.literal: Just then came heavy rain and wind; trees were uprooted and tiles flew.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a violent storm broke; trees were uprooted and roof tiles went flying.

sentences.zh: 兵相接，有屠者墨君和袒而薄賊，眾披靡，乃挾镕逾城入。

translations.literal: As the armies clashed, a butcher named Mo Junhe bared his torso and pressed close on the rebels; the crowd scattered in defeat, and he then seized Rong and carried him over the wall into the city.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies clashed, a butcher named Mo Junhe stripped to the waist and charged the rebels head-on. The enemy ranks broke and fled, and he seized Rong and carried him over the wall into the city.

sentences.zh: 既免，賞千金，與第一區，約宥十死。

translations.literal: Once Rong was safe, he rewarded him with one thousand in gold, granted him the finest district, and pledged pardon for ten capital offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Once Rong was safe, he rewarded Junhe with a thousand strings of gold, granted him the finest district in the city, and pledged pardon for ten capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 匡威走東園，兵圍之，與從事李抱貞俱死。

translations.literal: Kuangwei fled to the East Garden; troops surrounded him, and he died together with his staff member Li Baozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei fled to the East Garden, but troops surrounded him there. He and his aide Li Baozhen were both killed.

sentences.zh: 明日，镕以禮斂匡威，素服哭諸廷，遣使告匡籌。

translations.literal: The next day Rong buried Kuangwei with full rites, wore unadorned garb and wept before the court, and sent a messenger to inform Kuangchou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Rong buried Kuangwei with full honors, appeared at court in plain mourning dress to weep for him, and sent a messenger to notify Kuangchou.

sentences.zh: 匡籌怒，移書詰兄所以死狀，表天子請討镕，詔止之。

translations.literal: Kuangchou was enraged; he sent a letter demanding the circumstances of his brother's death, memorialized the Son of Heaven requesting a campaign against Rong, and an edict stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangchou was furious. He sent a letter demanding an account of his brother's death, memorialized the emperor requesting a punitive campaign against Rong, and the court ordered him to stand down.

sentences.zh: 又詔朱全忠平幽、鎮怨。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Zhu Quanzhong to settle the grievances between You and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered Zhu Quanzhong to settle the feud between Youzhou and Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 克用聞匡威死，自率兵傅城下。

translations.literal: Keyong heard that Kuangwei was dead and personally led troops to press against the foot of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Keyong learned of Kuangwei's death, he personally led an army to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 镕大驚，納縑二十萬，乃退。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly alarmed; he submitted two hundred thousand in silk and only then did Keyong withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was terrified. He sent two hundred thousand bolts of silk as tribute, and Keyong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 匡籌攻樂壽、武強，克用出縛馬關，敗鎮兵於平山，因進攻镕外壘。

translations.literal: Kuangchou attacked Leshou and Wuqiang. Keyong came out through Fuma Pass, defeated the Zhen troops at Pingshan, and then advanced to attack Rong's outer fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangchou attacked Leshou and Wuqiang. Keyong marched out through Fuma Pass, routed the Zhenzhou army at Pingshan, and then pressed on against Rong's outer fortifications.

sentences.zh: 镕內失幽州助，因乞盟，進幣五十萬，歸糧二十萬，請出兵助討存孝，乃得解。

translations.literal: Rong had internally lost You Prefecture's aid; he therefore sought alliance, sent gifts of five hundred thousand, returned two hundred thousand in grain, and requested troops to help attack Cunxiao—only then was he relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost Youzhou's support, Rong sued for peace. He sent five hundred thousand strings in gifts, returned two hundred thousand bushels of grain, and asked for troops to help attack Cunxiao—and only then was the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 克用屯欒城，存信屯琉璃陂，為邢人夜襲其營，存信軍亂，不克追。

translations.literal: Keyong encamped at Luancheng and Cunxin at Liuli Embankment. Men of Xing raided the camp by night; Cunxin's army fell into disorder and could not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong encamped at Luancheng while Cunxin held Liuli Embankment. Xingzhou troops raided the camp by night, throwing Cunxin's army into disorder so that he could not give chase.

sentences.zh: 克用進薄邢，環城為溝堞，欲示久圍者；

translations.literal: Keyong advanced close to Xing, ringed the city with moat and rampart, intending to show that he meant a long siege;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong pressed close to Xingzhou and began ringing the city with moats and ramparts, signaling his intent to settle in for a long siege;

sentences.zh: 城中兵數出，溝壘不可成。

translations.literal: troops from within the city sortied repeatedly, and the moat and fortifications could not be completed.
translations.idiomatic: but the garrison sortied again and again, and the moat and fortifications could never be finished.

sentences.zh: 裨將袁奉韜紿存孝曰：「君所畏唯王耳，王欲溝堞成則西歸，公何不聽之？」

translations.literal: The adjutant Yuan Fengtao deceived Cunxiao, saying: "What you fear is only the Prince. Once the moat and rampart are complete he intends to return west—why not let him have his way?"
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Yuan Fengtao deceived Cunxiao, saying, "Your only fear is the Prince himself. Once the moat and rampart are finished he means to march west—why not let him proceed?"

sentences.zh: 存孝兵不出，壘成，攻益急，城中食盡。

translations.literal: Cunxiao's troops did not sally forth; the fortifications were completed, the assault grew ever fiercer, and food within the city was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao kept his troops inside. The fortifications were completed, the assault grew fiercer still, and the city's food ran out.

sentences.zh: 存孝登城哭曰：「我誤計，使我生見王，死不恨！」

translations.literal: Cunxiao ascended the wall and wept, saying: "I miscalculated—let me see the Prince alive and I shall die without regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao climbed the wall and wept, "I chose wrongly. Let me see the Prince while I still live, and I will die without regret!"

sentences.zh: 克用遣家嫗招之，存孝出，泥首言為存信誣構，克用曰：「爾與镕書，罵我多矣！」

translations.literal: Keyong sent a household nurse to summon him. Cunxiao came out, kowtowed with his head in the mud, and said Cunxin had framed him. Keyong said: "In your letters with Rong you cursed me often enough!"
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent an old nurse from his household to summon him. Cunxiao came out, kowtowed with his face in the dirt, and said Cunxin had framed him. Keyong said, "In your letters with Rong you cursed me often enough!"

sentences.zh: 軒而屍於市。

translations.literal: He had him dragged through the market and his corpse displayed.
translations.idiomatic: He had him dragged through the market and his corpse put on public display.

sentences.zh: 光化中，全忠討幽州劉仁恭，镕遣兵屯蓚城，俄而仁恭敗，擊其歸，得十八。

translations.literal: During the Guanghua era, Quanzhong campaigned against Liu Rengong of You Prefecture. Rong sent troops to encamp at Tiaocheng. Before long Rengong was defeated; Rong struck his retreat and captured eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guanghua era, Quanzhong campaigned against Liu Rengong of Youzhou. Rong sent troops to hold Tiaocheng. When Rengong was defeated soon after, Rong struck his retreating column and took eighteen heads.

sentences.zh: 全忠既取邢、洺、礠，又得潞，因圖河東。

translations.literal: Quanzhong, having already taken Xing, Ming, and Ci, also gained Lu, and therefore plotted against Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong had already taken Xing, Ming, and Ci, and now gained Lu as well. He then turned his sights on Hedong.

sentences.zh: 使羅紹威諷镕絕太原，共尊全忠。

translations.literal: He had Luo Shaowei hint to Rong that he should break with Taiyuan and jointly honor Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He had Luo Shaowei suggest to Rong that he break with Taiyuan and join in honoring Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 镕猗違，全忠不悅。

translations.literal: Rong hesitated and prevaricated; Quanzhong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Rong hesitated and dragged his feet, and Quanzhong was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會克用將李嗣昭攻洺州，全忠自將擊走之，得镕與嗣昭書，全忠怒，引軍攻镕，次元氏。

translations.literal: It happened that Keyong's general Li Sizhao attacked Ming Prefecture; Quanzhong personally led troops to drive him off. He obtained letters between Rong and Sizhao. Quanzhong was enraged and led an army to attack Rong, first taking Yuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: When Keyong's general Li Sizhao attacked Mingzhou, Quanzhong marched out in person and drove him off. He captured correspondence between Rong and Sizhao, flew into a rage, and led an army against Rong, first taking Yuanshi.

sentences.zh: 镕謂其屬曰：「國危矣，奈何？」

translations.literal: Rong said to his staff: "The state is in peril—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Rong said to his staff, "The realm is in peril—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 周式請見全忠，可以口舌罷也，許之。
