translations.literal: Zhou Shi asked to see Quanzhong, saying he could dismiss the army with words alone; Rong permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shi asked to see Quanzhong, saying he could talk him into withdrawing. Rong agreed.

sentences.zh: 全忠迎折曰：「爾公朋附太原，今無赦矣！」

translations.literal: Quanzhong met him with a sharp rebuke, saying: "Your lord befriended Taiyuan—there is no pardon now!"
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong met him with a sharp rebuke. "Your master made common cause with Taiyuan—there is no pardon now!"

sentences.zh: 即出書示式曰：「嗣昭在者，宜速遣。」

translations.literal: He immediately produced the letters and showed Shi, saying: "If Sizhao is still here, he should be sent away at once."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately produced the letters and showed them to Shi. "If Sizhao is still here, send him away at once."

sentences.zh: 式曰：「王公所與和者，息人鋒鏑間耳。

translations.literal: Shi said: "What Lord Wang sought in making peace was merely to still blades and arrows between men.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "What Lord Wang sought in making peace was only to still the clash of blades and arrows.

sentences.zh: 況繼奉天子詔和解，能無一番紙墜北路乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, having again received the Son of Heaven's edict to reconcile, can there not be one letter that fell into northern hands?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he has again followed the emperor's edict calling for reconciliation—is it not possible that a single letter simply fell into northern hands?

sentences.zh: 太原與趙本無恩，嗣昭庸肯入耶？

translations.literal: Taiyuan and Zhao originally had no bond of favor—would Sizhao willingly enter?
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan and Zhao were never bound by any debt of gratitude—why would Sizhao willingly come here?

sentences.zh: 公為唐桓、文，方以仁義成霸業，寧困人於險耶？」

translations.literal: You are the Huan and Wen of Tang, just now forming hegemony through benevolence and righteousness—would you trap a man in straits?"
translations.idiomatic: You are Tang's Huan and Wen, building a hegemony on benevolence and righteousness—would you corner a man in his hour of peril?"

sentences.zh: 全忠喜，把式袂曰：「吾特戲耳！」

translations.literal: Quanzhong was pleased; he grasped Shi's sleeve and said: "I was only jesting!"
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was delighted. He seized Shi's sleeve and said, "I was only jesting!"

sentences.zh: 延入帳中，議脩好。

translations.literal: He invited him into the tent to discuss restoring good relations.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Shi into his tent to discuss restoring friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 镕以幣二十萬賂師，遣子昭祚質仕全忠府，全忠因妻之。

translations.literal: Rong used two hundred thousand in gifts to bribe the army, sent his son Zhaozuo as hostage to serve in Quanzhong's yamen, and Quanzhong gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sent two hundred thousand strings in gifts to buy off the army, dispatched his son Zhaozuo as a hostage to serve in Quanzhong's headquarters, and Quanzhong gave him a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 镕判官張澤謀曰：「失火之家，不可恃遠救。

translations.literal: Rong's judge Zhang Ze plotted, saying: "A house that has caught fire cannot rely on distant rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's aide Zhang Ze advised, "A house already ablaze cannot count on help from far away.

sentences.zh: 今定密邇，與太原親，宜使全忠圖之。」

translations.literal: Now Ding is close at hand and intimate with Taiyuan—it is fitting to have Quanzhong target it."
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou lies close by and is on intimate terms with Taiyuan. Quanzhong should be urged to move against it."

sentences.zh: 镕遣式使全忠，全忠乃取定州，王郜遂奔太原。

translations.literal: Rong sent Shi as envoy to Quanzhong; Quanzhong then took Ding Prefecture, and Wang Gao fled to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sent Shi as envoy to Quanzhong. Quanzhong then seized Dingzhou, and Wang Gao fled to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 镕母何，有婦德，訓镕嚴。

translations.literal: Rong's mother He possessed wifely virtue and trained Rong strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's mother, Lady He, was a woman of exemplary virtue and raised him with strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 至母亡，镕始黷貨財，姬侍千人，儀服僭上。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Rong then began to covet goods and wealth, kept a thousand concubines, and his raiment and regalia surpassed the emperor's.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, Rong began to hoard wealth, kept a thousand concubines, and dressed in regalia that exceeded imperial rank.

sentences.zh: 又以房山有西王母祠，數遊覽，妄求長年事，逾月不還。

translations.literal: Also, because Fangshan had a shrine to the Queen Mother of the West, he repeatedly toured there, vainly seeking the arts of long life, and for more than a month did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fangshan held a shrine to the Queen Mother of the West, he visited it again and again, vainly seeking the secret of long life, and stayed away for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 始廷湊賤微時，鄴有道士為卜，得《乾之坤》，曰：「君將有土。」

translations.literal: When Tingcou was still lowly and obscure, a Daoist at Ye divined for him and obtained Qian changing to Kun, saying: "My lord will possess territory."
translations.idiomatic: When Tingcou was still obscure and lowly, a Daoist at Ye cast hexagrams for him and obtained Qian changing to Kun. "My lord will come into land," he said."

sentences.zh: 及得鎮，迎事甚謹。

translations.literal: When he obtained the command, he welcomed and served the Daoist with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: When he gained the command, he welcomed the Daoist back and served him with the greatest respect.

sentences.zh: 復問壽幾何？

translations.literal: He again asked how long his life would be.
translations.idiomatic: He asked again how long he would live.

sentences.zh: 子孫幾何？」

translations.literal: How many descendants?"
translations.idiomatic: How many descendants would he have?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「公三十年後，當有二王。」

translations.literal: The answer was: "Thirty years after you, there will be two kings."
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist answered, "Thirty years after you, there will be two kings."

sentences.zh: 已而廷湊立十三年死，蓋廋文也，景崇、镕皆王。

translations.literal: Before long Tingcou established rule and died in the thirteenth year—it was cryptic wording; Jingchong and Rong were both Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou held power for thirteen years and then died—the prophecy was cryptic wordplay: Jingchong and Rong were both Wangs.

sentences.zh: 廷湊嘗使至河陽，醉寢於路，有過其所者視之曰：「非常人也！」

translations.literal: Tingcou once had an envoy travel to Heyang; drunk, he slept on the road. Someone passing by looked at him and said: "This is no ordinary man!"
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou once sent an envoy to Heyang. The man got drunk and fell asleep on the road. A passerby looked him over and said, "This is no ordinary man!"

sentences.zh: 從者以告廷湊，馳及之，問其故，曰：「吾見君鼻之息，左若龍，右若虎，子孫當王百年。

translations.literal: The attendants told Tingcou; he galloped after the man and asked the reason. The man said: "I saw the breath from your nose—on the left like a dragon, on the right like a tiger; your descendants will reign as kings for a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants told Tingcou, who galloped after the man and asked what he meant. The man said, "I saw the breath from your nostrils—dragon-like on the left, tiger-like on the right. Your descendants will hold kingship for a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 家有大樹，覆及堂，公興矣，」及害弘正，而樹適庇寢。

translations.literal: Your house has a great tree whose shade reaches the hall—you will rise." When he killed Hongzheng, the tree happened to shade the bedroom.
translations.idiomatic: Your house has a great tree whose shade reaches the hall—you will rise to power." When he murdered Hongzheng, a great tree happened to shade his sleeping chamber.

sentences.zh: 自廷湊訖镕，凡百年。

translations.literal: From Tingcou to Rong, altogether one hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: From Tingcou to Rong, a full century passed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：朱滔、王武俊南面稱王，地聯交昵。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun declared themselves kings in the south; their territories were linked and their relations intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun declared themselves kings in the south, their territories adjoining and their alliance close.

sentences.zh: 及泚僭天子，滔將應之，當時危矣。

translations.literal: When Ci usurped the title of Son of Heaven, Tao was about to respond; at that time the peril was grave.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci seized the imperial title, Tao was poised to join him—the realm stood at the brink.

sentences.zh: 賈林以一語寤武俊，軋兵相仇，折幽、薊之銳，泚失其朋，不出孤城，終底覆夷，用林之功，賞不及身，德宗為不明哉！

translations.literal: Jia Lin with a single phrase awakened Wujun; their armies turned against one another as enemies, blunting the edge of You and Ji. Ci lost his allies, dared not leave his lone city, and ultimately came to utter ruin. For Lin's merit, reward did not reach him in life—was Emperor Dezong not unenlightened!
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lin awakened Wujun with a single sentence. Their armies turned on each other, blunting the fighting edge of You and Ji. Ci lost his allies, never dared leave his isolated city, and was ultimately destroyed. Lin's service went unrewarded in his lifetime—was Emperor Dezong not blind to merit!
